G4012.d:
περί, 
prep. with genitive, accusative (in cl. also with dative; cf. M, Pr., 105f.),  
with radical sense round about (as distinct from ἀμφί, on both sides).  
  I. C. genitive, 
  1. of place, about (poët.). 
  2. Causal, about, on account of, concerning, in reference to: Matt.2:8, Mark.1:44, Luke.4:38, John.16:26, Acts.28:21, al. mult.; τὰ περί, with genitive, the things concerning one, one's state or case: Mark.5:27, Acts.1:3 28:15, Eph.6:22, al.; at the beginning of a sentence, περί, regarding, as to, 1 Cor.7:1, al.; in the sense on account of (Matt.26:28, 1 Cor.1:13, al.), often with ὑπέρ as variant (cf. M, Pr., 105). 
  II. C. accusative, 
  1. of place, about, around: Matt.3:4, Mark.1:6, Luke.13:8, Acts.22:6, al.; οἱ περί, with accusative of person(s), of one's associates, friends, etc., Mark.4:10, Luke.22:49, John.11:19, Acts.13:13; οἱ περὶ τ. τοιαῦτα ἐργάται, Acts.19:25; metaphorically, about, as to, concerning: 1 Tim.1:19 6:4 2 Tim.2:18 3:8, Titus.2:7; τὰ περὶ ἐμέ, Phil.2:23; αἱ περὶ τ. λοιπὰ ἐπιθυμίαι, Mark.4:19. 
  2. Of time, in a loose reckoning, about, near: Matt.20:3, 5 6, 9 27:46, Mark.6:48, Acts.10:3, 9 22:6. 
  III. In composition: round about (περιβάλλω, περίκειμαι), beyond, over and above (περιποιέω, περιλείπω), to excess (περιεργάζομαι, περισσεύω). 
 (AS)

G4052.d:

 SYN.: πλεονάζω  (AS)

G4063.d:
περι-τρέχω 
 [in LXX: Amo.8:12, Jer.5:1 (שׁוּט pi.) * ;] 
to run about: with accusative loc., Mark.6:55.†
 (AS)

G4064.d:
περι-φέρω 
 [in LXX: Ecc.7:8 (7) (הָלַל po.), al. ;] 
to carry about: Mark.6:55, 2 Cor.4:10. Pass., metaphorically: Eph.4:14.†
 (AS)

G4065.d:
περι-φρονέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: 4Ma.6:9 4Mac 14:1 * ;] 
  1. to examine on all sides, consider carefully (Aristoph.). 
  2. = ὑπερφρονέω, to have thouphts beyond, to despise (Thuc., Plut., al.; 4Mac, ll. with) : Titus.2:15.†
 (AS)

G4066.d:
περί-χωρος, -ον 
 [in LXX: chiefly (ἡ π.) for כִּכָּר ;] 
round about, neighbouring (Dem., Plut., al.). In LXX and NT, as subst., ἡ π. (sc. γῆ), the region round about: Matt.14:35, Mark.1:28, Luke.4:14, 37 7:17 8:37, Acts.14:6; ἡ π. τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, Luke.3:3; by meton. for the people of the same region, Matt.3:5.†
 (AS)

G4067.d:
περί-ψημα, -τος, τό
 (περιψράω, to wipe off all round), [in LXX:  Tob.5:18 * ;] 
that which is wiped off, offscouring: metaphorically (assoc. with περικάθαρμα, which see), 1 Cor.4:13 (and so prob., To, l.with, as EV; but see Thayer, see word, for the meaning expiation, ransom, in To; and cf. LS, see word κάθαρμα; Lft., Notes, 200 f., and on Ign., Eph., 8).†
 (AS)

G4068.d:
περπερεύοραι
 (περπερος, vainglorious) 
to boast or vaunt oneself: 1 Cor.13:4 (elsewhere. only in Antonin.; see Abbott, Essays, 87).†
 (AS)

G4069.d:
1. Persian , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 
2. as Substantive, (.] (entry γῆ); Persis, Persia , now Farsistan , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. (entry γυνή); a Persian woman , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. (entry χλαῖνα); a Persian cloak , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
 (ML)

G4070.d:
πέρυσι 
 adv. (πέρας), 
last year, a year ago: ἀπὸ π. (as in π. see Deiss., BS, 221; LAE, 70), 2 Cor.8:10 9:2.†
 (AS)

G4071.d:
πετεινός, -ή, -όν
 (πέτομαι), [in LXX chiefly for עוֹף ;] 
in trag., Ion. and late writers, winged, flying; as subst., τὸ π., a winged fowl, a bird: pl., Matt.6:26 8:20 13:4, 32, Mark.4:4, 32, Luke.8:5 9:58 12:24 13:19, Acts.10:12 11:6, Rom.1:23, Jas.3:7.†
 (AS)

G4072.d:
πέτομαι 
 [in LXX chiefly for עוּף ;] 
to fly: Rev.4:7 8:13 12:14 14:6 19:17 (Rec. πετάομαι, which see).†
 πετάομαι, 
 [in LXX: Deu.4:17 * ;] 
false form of ποτάομαι, poët., frequentat. of πέτομαι (Aristoph., al.), Rec. for πέτομαι (which see, cf. Veitch, see word) 
 (AS)

G4073.d:
πέτρα, -ας, ἡ 
 [in LXX chiefly for סֶלַע, צוּר ;] 
a rock, i.e. a mass of live rock as distinct from πέτρος, a detached stone or boulder : Matt.7:24-25 27:51, 60 Mark.15:46, Luke.6:48 8:6, 13; of a hollow rock, a cave, Rev.6:15-16 (of. Isa.2:10, al.). Metaphorical, Matt.16:18 (on the meaning, see Hort, Eccl., 16 ff., but cf. also ICC, in l), 1 Cor.10:4; = πέτρος, Rom.9:33, 1 Pet.2:8" (LXX) .†
 (AS)

G4074.d:
Πέτρος, -ου, ὁ (i.e. a stone, see: πέτρα, Κηφᾶς), 
 Simon Peter, the Apostle: Matt.4:18 10:2, Mark.3:16, Luke.5:8, John.1:41, 43, al. 
 (AS)

G4075.d:
πετρώδης, -ες
 (πέτρα, εἶδος), 
rock-like, rocky, stony: τὸ, τὰ π., of shallow soil with underlying rock, Matt.13:5, 20, Mark.4:5, 16.†
 (AS)

G4076.d:
πήγανον, -ου, τό 
 περισσότερον, -ως, see: περισσῶς 
  περισσῶς
  adv. (περισσός) [in LXX: Ps.31:23 (יֶתֶר -עַל), Da TH Dan.7:7, 19 8:9 (יַתִּיר, יֶתֶר) 2Ma.8:27 2Mac 12:44 A * ;] 
beyond measure, exceedingly, abundantly: Matt.27:23, Mark.10:26 15:14, Acts.26:11. Compar. 
  (a) περισσότερον (see: περισσός); 
  (b) περισσοτέρως: 2 Cor.1:12 2:4 7:15 11:23, Gal.1:14, Phil.1:14, 1 Thess.2:17, Heb.2:1 13:19; π. μᾶλλον, 2 Cor.7:13; opposite to ἧττον, 2 Cor.12:15.†
 (AS)

G4077.d:
πηγή, -ῆς, ἡ 
 [in LXX chiefly for עַיִן, also for מָקוֹר, etc. ;] 
a spring, fountain : Jas.3:11, 2 Pet.2:17; τ. δάτων, Rev.8:10 14:7 16:4; of a well fed by a spring, John.4:6; π. τοῦ αἵματος, of a flow of blood, Mark.5:29; metaphorically, John.4:14, Rev.7:17 21:6.†
 (AS)

G4078.d:
πήγνυμι 
 [in LXX chiefly for נָטָה, also for תָּקַע, etc. ;] 
to make fast, to fix; of tents, to pitch: Heb.8:2 (cf. προσ-πήγνυμι).†
 (AS)

G4079.d:
πηδάλιον, -συ, τό
 (πηδός, the blade of an oar), 
a rudder: Jas.3:4; pl., Acts.27:40.†
 (AS)

G4080.d:
πηλίκος, -η, -ον 
 [in LXX: Zec.2:2 (6) (כָּמַהּ), 4Ma.15:22 * ;] 
interrog., how large, how great ? (prop., of magnitude, as πόσος of quantity): in exclamations, = ἡλίκος (see Bl., § 51, 4), Gal.6:11; of personal greatness, Heb.7:4.†
 (AS)

G4081.d:
πηλός, οῦ, ἁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for חֹמֶר, טִיט ] 
  1. clay, as used by a potter: Rom.9:21 (cf. Isa.29:16, al.). 
  2. - βόρβορος, wet clay, mud: John.9:6, 11 9:14-15 †
 (AS)

G4082.d:
πἡρα, -ας, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Jdth.10:5 13:10, 15 * ;] 
a leathern pouch for  victuals, etc., a wallet (Deiss. thinks an alms-bag, see LAE, 108 ff.): Matt.10:10, Mark.6:8, Luke.9:3 10:4 22:35-36.†
 (AS)

G4083.d:
πῆχυς, -εως genitive pl., -ῶν (for Att.. -εων, see WH, App., 157; Thackeray, Gr., 151; Deiss., BS, 153), 
 [in LXX chiefly and frequently for אַמָּה ;] 
  1. the forearm (Hom.). 
  2. As a measure of length, a cubit: Matt.6:27, Luke.12:25, John.21:8, Rev.21:17.†
 (AS)

G4084.d:
πιάζω
 (cf. MGr. πιάνω; see Kennedy, Sources, 155), Doric and late Att.. for πιέζω in its later senses [in LXX: Sng.2:15 (אָחַז), Sir.23:21 * ;] 
  1. to lay hold of: Acts.3:7 (Theocr.). 
  2. to take, capture, apprehend: John.7:30, 32 7:44 8:20 10:39 11:57 21:3, 10 Acts.12:4, 2 Cor.11:32, Rev.19:20 (see MM, xx).†
 (AS)

G4085.d:
πιέζω 
 [in LXX : Mic.6:15 (דָּרַךְ)* ;] 
  1. to press, press down or to­gether: Luke.6:38 (cl). 
  2. Later, to seize (see: πιάζω).†
 (AS)

G4086.d:
πιθανολογία, -ας, ἡ 
 (πιθανός, persuasive, plausible), 
in cl. (Plat), 
 the use of probable arguments, as opposite to demonstration (ἀπόδειξις); hence, persuasive speech: Col.2:4 (see ICC, in l).†
 (AS)

G4087.d:
πικραίνω
 (πικρός), [in LXX for מָרַד, קָצַף, etc. ;] 
to make bitter: Rev.10:9; pass., Rev.8:11 10:10; metaphorically, to embitter (LXX) : pass., before πρός, Col.3:19.†
 (AS)

G4089.d:
πικρός, -ά, -όν
 (poët. in cl.), [in LXX chiefly for מַר ;] 
  1. sharp, pointed. 
  2. sharp to the senses; of taste, bitter: opposite to γλυκύ, Jas.3:11; metaphorically, harsh, bitter: Jas.3:14 
 (AS)

G4090.d:
πικρῶς 
 adv. (πικρός), [in LXX for מַר, מָרַר pi. ;] 
bitterly: metaphorically, (cf. πικρὸν δάκρυον, Hom.), ἔκλαυσε π., Matt.26:75, Luke.22:62 (see MM, xviii, see word παρακολουθέω).†
 (AS)

G4091.d:
Πειλᾶτος (Rec. Πιλάτος, Tr., -ᾶτος, see WH, App., 155), -ου, ὁ, 
 Pontius Pilate: Matt.27:2, Mark.15:1, Luke.3:1, John.18:29, Acts.3:13, 1 Tim.6:13, al
 (AS)

G4092.d:
πίμπρημι
 (in cl. prose, rare in the simple form), [in LXX: Num.5:21-22, 27 (צָבֶה) * ;] 
  1. to blow, burn. 
  2. Later, to cause to swell; mid., of parts of the body, to become swollen (LXX) : Acts.28:6 (cf. ἐμπίπρημι).†
 (AS)

G4093.d:
πινακίδιον, -ου, τό
 (dimin. of πινακίς, which see), [in Sm.: Eze.9:2 * ;] 
a writing tablet: Luke.1:63.†
 (AS)

G4095.d:
πίνω 
 [in LXX chiefly for שָׁתָה ;] 
to drink: absol., Luke.2:19, John.4:7, al.; with accusative of thing(s), Matt.6:26, 31 Mark.14:25, al.; of habitual use, Luke.1:15, Rom.14:21, al.; by meton., τὸ ποτήριον, 1 Cor.10:21, al.; of the earth absorbing rain (Hdt., al.), Heb.6:7; spiritually, of the blood of Christ, John.6:53-54, 56; before ἐκ (of the vessel), Matt.26:27, al.; id. (of the drink; Bl., § 36, 1), Matt.26:29, John.4:13-14 Rev.14:10, al.; ἀπό, Luke.22:18 (cf. ἀπο-, συν-πίνω; on the form πίεσαι, Luke.17:8, see Bl., § 21, 8, and on the contr. aor. πεῖν, M, Pr., 44 f., Thackeray, Gr., 63 f.) 
 (AS)

G4096.d:
πιότης, -ητος, ἡ
 (πίων, fat), [in LXX chiefly for דֶּשֶׁן ;] 
fatness: Rom.11:17.†
 (AS)

G4097.d:
πιπράσκω 
 [in LXX chiefly for מָכַר ni. ;] 
to sell: with accusative of thing(s), Matt.13:46 (on this pf., see Bl., § 59, 5), Acts.2:45 4:34 5:4; with genitive (of price), Matt.26:9, Mark.14:5, John.12:5; with accusative of person(s) (of slavery), Matt.18:25; hence metaphorically, Rom.7:14 (cf. 4Ki.17:17, 1Ma.1:15, al.).†
 (AS)

G4098.d:
πίπτω 
 [in LXX chiefly for נָפַל ;] 
to fall; 
  1. of descent, to fall, fall down or from: before ἐπί, with accusative loc., Matt.10:29, al.; εἰς, Matt.15:14, al.; ἐς μέσῳ, with genitive, Luke.8:7; παρὰ τ. ὁδόν, Matt.13:4, Mark.4:4, Luke.8:5; before ἀπό, Matt.15:27, al.; ἐκ, Mark.13:25, Luke.10:18, Rev.8:10 9:1. Metaphorical: ὁ ἥλιος, before ἐπί, Rev.7:16; ἀχλὺς κ. σκότος, Acts.13:11; ὁ κλῆρος, Acts.1:26; ὑπὸ κρίσιν, Jas.5:12. 
  2. Of prostration, 
  (a) of persons, to fall prostrate, prostrate oneself: χαμαί John.18:6; before ἐπί, with accusative, Matt.17:6, Acts.9:4; id. with genitive, Mark.9:20; πρὸς τ. πόδας, Acts.5:10, Rev.1:17; πεσὼν ἐξέψυξε, Acts.5:5; of supplication, homage or worship: πρὸς (παρὰ, ἐπὶ) τ. πὸδας, Mark.5:22, Luke.8:41, Acts.10:25, al.; π. καὶ προσκυνεῖν, Rev.5:14 19:4; ptcp. with προσκυνεῖν, Matt.2:11, al.; ἐνώπιον, Rev.4:10 5:8; ἐπὶ πρόσωπον, Matt.26:39, al.; 
  (b) of things, to fall, fall down: Matt.21:44, Luke.23:30; of falling to ruin and destruction, Matt.7:25, Acts.15:16, Heb.11:30; ἔπεσε (timeless aorist; M, Pr.,134), Rev.18:2. Metaphorical: Rom.11:11; πόθεν πέπτωκας, Rev.2:5; opposite to ἑστόναι, 1 Cor.10:12; to στήκειν, Rom.14:4; of virtues, 1 Cor.13:8; of precepts, Luke.16:17. 
 (cf. ἀνα-, ἀντι-, ἀπο-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, παρα-, περι-, προσ-, συν-πίπτω.) 
συν-πίπτω (Rec. συμπ-), 
 [in LXX for נָפַל, etc. ;] 
to fall together, fall in, etc.: of a house (cf. MM, xxiv), Luke.6:49.†
 (AS)

G4099.d:
Πισιδία, -ας, ι 
 Pisidia, a region of Asia Minor: Acts.14:24 
 (AS)

G4100.d:
πιστεύω, 
 [in LXX chiefly for אמן hi. ;] 
  1. intrans., to have faith (in), to believe; in cl., with accusative, dative, in NT also with prep, (on the significance of the various constructions, see M, Pr., 67f.; Vau. on Rom.4:5; Ellic. on 1 Tim.1:16; Abbott, JV, 19-80): absol., Matt.24:23, 26 Mark.13:21, 1 Cor.11:18; with accusative of thing(s), Acts.13:41, 1 Cor.13:7; with dative of person(s) (to believe what one says), Mrk.16:[13, 14], 1 John.4:1; τ. ψεύδει, 2 Thess.2:11; περί . . . ὅτι, John.9:18; esp. and most frequently with reference to religious belief: absol., Matt.8:13, Mark.5:36, Luke.8:50, John.11:40, al.; before ὅτι, Matt.9:28, al.; with dative (see supr., and cf. DB, i, 829a), John.3:12 5:24 6:30 8:31, Acts.16:34, Gal.3:6" (LXX), 2 Tim.1:12, 1 John.5:10, al.; with prep., (expressing personal trust and reliance  as distinct from mere credence or belief; see M, Pr., l.with; DB, i, 829b), to believe in or on: ἐν (Psa.77 (78):22, al.), Mark.1:15 (see Swete, in l.); εἰς, Matt.18:6, John.2:11 (see Westc., in l.), and freq., Acts.10:43 19:4, Rom.10:14, Gal.2:16, Phil.1:29, I John.5:10, 1 Pet.1:8; εἰς τ. ὄνομα, John.1:12 2:23 3:18, 1 John.5:13; ἐπί, with accusative, Matt.27:42, Acts.9:42 11:17 16:31 22:19, Rom.4:5; ἐπί, with dative, Rom.9:33 (LXX) 10:11 (ib.), 1 Tim.1:16, 1 Pet.2:6" (LXX) ; ptcp. pres., οἱ π., as subst., Acts.2:44, Rom.3:22, 1 Cor.1:21, al.; aor., Mrk.16:[16], Acts.4:32; pf., Acts.19:18 21:20 (on Johannine use of the tenses of π., see Westc, Epp. Jo., 120). 
  2. Trans., to entrust: with accusative and dative, Luke.16:11, John.2:24; pass., to be entrusted with: with accusative, Rom.3:2, 1 Cor.9:17, Gal.2:7, 1 Thess.2:4 (see Lft., Notes, 21f.), 1 Tim.1:11, Titus.1:3.
 (AS)

G4101.d:
πιστικός, -ή, -όν (πίστις), 
  1. having the gift of persuasion (Plat., Gorg., 455A). 
  2. 
  (a) of persons, faithful, trusty (Plut.); 
  (b) of things, trustworthy, genuine: νάρδος π., Mark.14:3, John.12:3.
 † (AS)

G4102.d:
πίστις, -εως, ἡ 
 (πείθω), [in LXX chiefly for אֱמוּנָה ;] 
  1. in active sense, faith, belief, trust, confidence, in NT always of religious faith in God or Christ or spiritual things: Matt.8:10, Luke.5:20, Acts.14:9, Rom.1:8, 1 Cor.2:5, 2 Cor.1:24, 1 Tim.1:5, al.; with genitive obj., Mark.11:22, Acts.3:16, Rom.3:22, Gal.2:16, Eph.3:12, Jas.2:1, al.; with prep., ἐν, Rom.3:25, Gal.3:26, Eph.1:15, Col.1:24, 1 Tim.1:14 3:13, 2 Tim.1:13 3:15, 2 Pet.1:1; εἰς, Acts.20:21 24:24 26:18, Col.2:5, 1 Pet.1:21; πρός, 1 Thess.1:8, Phm 5; ἐπί, with accusative Heb.6:1; ἐν τῇ π. στήκειν (εἶναι, μένειν), 1 Cor.16:13, 1 Cor.13:5, 1 Tim.2:15; ὑπακοὴ τῆς π., Rom.1:5 16:26; ὁ ἐκ π., Rom.3:26 4:16, Gal.3:12; διὰ (τῆς) π., Rom.3:30, Gal.2:16, Phil.3:9. By meton., objectively, that which is the object or content of belief, the faith: Acts.6:7 14:22, Gal.1:23 3:23 6:10, Phil.1:26, 27 Ju 3, 20, and perh. also Acts.13:8 16:5, Rom.1:5 and 16:26 (see supr.), 1 Cor.16:13, Col.1:23, 2 Thess.3:2 (Lft., Notes, 125), 1 Tim.1:19 3:9 4:1, 6 5:8 6:10, 12, 2 Tim.3:8 4:7 Titus.1:4, 13 3:15, 1 Pet.5:9. 
  2. In passive sense, 
  (a) fidelity, faithfulness: Matt.23:23, Gal.5:22; ἡ π. τοῦ θεοῦ, Rom.3:3; 
  (b) objectively, plighted faith, a pledge of fidelity: 1 Tim.5:12. (On the various shades of meaning in which the word is used in NT, see esp. ICC on Rom.1:17, pp. 31ff.; Lft., Ga., 154ff.; Stevens, Th. NT, 422, 515ff.; DB, i, 830ff.; Cremer, see word) 
 (AS)

G4103.d:
πιστός, -ή, -όν
 (πείθω), [in LXX chiefly for אָמַן ;] 
  I. Pass., to be trusted or believed; 
  1. of persons, trusty, faithful : Matt.24:45 25:21, 23 Luke.12:42, Acts.16:15, 1 Cor.4:2 4:17 7:25, Eph.1:1 6:21, Col.1:2, 7 4:7, 9, 1 Tim.1:12, 2 Tim.2:2, Heb.2:17 3:2, 5, 1 Pet.5:12, Rev.2:13 19:11; of God, 1 Cor.1:9 10:13, 2 Cor.1:18, 1 Thess.5:24, 2 Thess.3:3, Heb.10:23 11:11, 2 Tim.2:13, 1 John.1:9, 1 Pet.4:19; before ἐν, Luke.16:10-12 19:17, 1 Tim.3:11; ἐπί, with accusative, Matt.25:23; ἄχρι θανάτου, Rev.2:10; ὁ μάρτυς ὁ π., Rev.1:5; id. καὶ ἀληθινός, Rev.3:14. 
  2. Of things, trustworthy, reliable, sure: Acts.13:34, 1 Tim.1:15 3:1 4:9, 2 Tim.2:11, Titus.1:9 3:8, Rev.21:5 22:6. 
  II. Act., believing, trusting, relying: Acts.16:1, 2 Cor.6:15, Gal.3:9, 1 Tim.4:10 5:16 6:2, Titus.1:6, Rev.17:14; pl., Acts.10:45, 1 Tim.4:3 4:12; opposite to ἄπιστος, John.20:27; π. εἰς θεόν, 1 Pet.1:21; π. ποιεῖν, III Jn 5. 
 (On the difficulty of choosing in some cases between the active and the passive meaning, see Lft., Gal., 157.) †
 (AS)

G4104.d:
πιστόω, -ῶ
 (πιστός), [in LXX chiefly for אָמֵן ni. ;] 
to make  trustworthy (Thuc., 3Ki.1:36), hence, to establish (1Ch.17:14). Pass. and mid., to be assured of: with accusative of thing(s), 2 Tim.3:14.†
 (AS)

G4105.d:
πλανάω, -ῶ
 (πλάνη), [in LXX chiefly for תָּעָה ;] 
to cause to wander, lead astray. Pass., to go astray, wander: Matt.18:12-13 Heb.11:38, 1 Pet.2:25 (cf. Isa.53:6). Metaphorical, to lead astray, deceive: with accusative of person(s), Matt.24:4-5, 11 24:24, Mark.13:5-6, John.7:12, 2 Tim.3:13; 1 John.1:8 Jn 2:26 Jn 3:7, Rev.2:20 12:9 13:14 19:20 20:3, 8 20:10; pass., to be led astray, to err: Matt.22:29, Mark.12:24, 27, Luke.21:8, John.7:47, 2 Tim.3:13, Titus.3:3, Heb.5:2, 2 Pet.2:15, Rev.18:23; τ. καρδίᾳ, Heb.3:10; ἀπὸ τ. ἀληθείας, Jas.5:19;μὴ πλανᾶσθε, 1 Cor.6:9 15:33, Gal.6:7. Jas.1:16 (cf. ἀπο-πλανάω).†
 (AS)

G4106.d:
πλάνη, -ης, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Pro.14:8 (מִרְמָה), Wis.1:12, al ;] 
a wandering. Metaphorical, a going astray, an error (in NT always with respect to morals or religion): Matt.27:64, Rom.1:27, Eph.4:14, 1 Thess.2:3, 2 Thess.2:11, Jas.5:20, 2 Pet.2:18 3:17 3:1-18; 1 John.4:6, Ju 11.†
 (AS)

G4107.d:
πλανήτης, -ου, ὁ
 (πλανάω), [in LXX: Hos.9:17 (נָדַד) * ;] 
= πλάνης, a wanderer: ἀστέρες π. (cl. planets), wandering stars, Ju 13 (WH, mg., -τες).†
 (AS)

G4108.d:
πλάνος, -ον 
 [in LXX: Job.19:4 (מְשׁוּגָה), Jer.23:32 * ;] 
  1. wandering. 
  2. leading astray, deceiving: πνεύματα π., 1 Tim.4:1. As subst., ὁ π., a deceiver, impostor: Matt.27:63, 2 Cor.6:8 6:1-18 2 John.1:7.†
 (AS)

G4109.d:
πλάξ, -ακός, ἡ 
 [in LXX for לוּחַ ;] 
anything flat and broad. 
  1. a plain (poët.). 
  2. In late writers (Luc., al.), a flat stone, a tablet: 2 Cor.3:3, Heb.9:4.†
 (AS)

G4110.d:
πλάσμα, -τος, τό
 (πλάσσω), [in LXX chiefly for יֵצֶר ;] 
that which is moulded or formed : Rom.9:20 (LXX).†
 (AS)

G4111.d:
πλάσσω 
 [in LXX chiefly for יָצַר ;] 
to form, mould: Rom.9:26 (LXX), 1 Tim.2:13.†
 (AS)

G4112.d:
πλαστός, -ή, -όν
 (πλάσσω), 
  1. formed, moulded (Hes., Plat., al.). 
  2. Metaphorical, made up, fabricated, feigned (Hdt., Xen., al.): 2 Pet.2:3.†
 (AS)

G4113.d:
πλατεία, -ας, ἡ, see: πλατύς.
  πλατύς, -εῖα, -ύ 
 [in LXX for רָחָב ;] 
broad: Matt.7:13. As subst., ἡ π. (sc. ὁδός), 
 [in LXX chiefly for רָחָב ;] 
a street: Matt.6:5 12:19" (LXX), Mark.6:56, WH, mg., Luke.10:10 13:26 14:21, Acts.5:15, Rev.11:8 21:21 22:2.†
 (AS)

G4114.d:
πλάτος, -ους, τό 
 [in LXX chiefly for רֹחַב ;] 
breadth: Eph.3:18, Rev.21:16; τ. π. τῆς γῆς (Hab.1:6, מֶרְחָב), Rev.20:9.†
 (AS)

G4115.d:
πλατύνω
 (πλατύς), [in LXX chiefly for רָחַב hi. ;] 
to make broad, enlarge, extend: with accusative of thing(s), Matt.23:5. Metaphorical (cf. Ps.119:32, al.), pass., ἡ καρδία, 2 Cor.6:11; ὑμεῖς, 2 Cor.6:13.†
 (AS)

G4116.d:
πλατύς, -εῖα, -ύ 
 [in LXX for רָחָב ;] 
broad: Matt.7:13. As subst., ἡ π. (sc. ὁδός), 
 [in LXX chiefly for רָחָב ;] 
a street: Matt.6:5 12:19" (LXX), Mark.6:56, WH, mg., Luke.10:10 13:26 14:21, Acts.5:15, Rev.11:8 21:21 22:2.†
 (AS)

G4117.d:
πλέγμα, -τος, τό
 (πλέκω), [in Aq., Th.: Isa.28:5 * ;] 
what is woven or twisted (as basket-work, nets, etc.); a braiding (sc. τριχῶν, cf. 1 Pet.3:3) : pl., 1 Tim.2:9.†
 (AS)

G4118.d:
πλεῖστος, πλείων, see: πολύς.
  πολύς, πολλή, πολύ, 
 [in LXX chiefly for רַב and cognate forms ;] 
  1. as adj., much, many, great, of number, space, degree, value, time, etc.: ἀριθμός, Acts.11:21; ὄχλος, Mark.5:24; θερισμός, Matt.9:37; χόρτος, John.6:10; χρόνος, Matt.25:19; γογγυσμός, John.7:12; πόνος, Col.4:13; δόξα, Matt.24:30; σιγή, Acts.21:40; pl., προφῆται, Matt.13:17; ὄχλοι, Matt.4:25; δαιμόνια, Mark.1:34; δυνάμεις, Matt.7:22, 
  2. As subst., pl. masc, πολλοί, many (persons): Matt.7:22, Mark.2:2, al.; with genitive partit., Matt.3:7, Luke.1:16, al.; before ἐκ, John.7:31, Acts.17:12; with art., οἱ π., the many, Matt.24:12, Rom.12:5, 1 Cor.10:17, 33 2 Cor.2:17; opposite to ὁ εἶς (Lft., Notes, 291), Rom.5:15, 19; neut. pl., πολλά: Matt.13:3, Mark.5:26, al.; accusative with adverbial force, Mark.1:45, Rom.16:6 (Deiss., LAE, 317), 1 Cor.16:12, Jas.3:2, al.; neut. sing., πολύ: Luke.12:48; adverbially, Mark.12:27, al.; πολλοῦ (genitive pret.), Matt.26:9; with compar. (Bl., §44, 5), π. σπουδαιότερον, 2 Cor.8:22; πολλῷ πλείους, John.4:41. 
 Compar., πλείων
, neut., πλεῖον and πλέον (see WH, App., 151), pl., πλείονες, -ας, -α, contr., πλείους, -ω (cf. Mayser, 69), more, greater; 
  1. as adj.: John.15:2, Acts.18:2o, Heb.3:3; before παρά, Heb.11:4 (cf. Westc, in l. Was ΠΛΙΟΝΑ here a primitive error for ΗΔΙΟΝΑ ?); pi., Acts.13:31, al.; with genitive compar., Matt.21:36; with num. (ἤ of comp. omitted), Acts.4:22 24:11, al. 
  2. As subst., οἱ π., the greater number: Acts.10:32 27:12, 1 Cor.10:5 15:6; also (Bl., §44, 3) others, more, the more: 2 Cor.2:6 4:15, Phil.1:14; πλείονα, Luke.11:53; πλειον, πλέον, Matt.20:10, 2 Tim.3:9; with genitive comp., Mk  12:43, Luke.21:3; π. Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε, Matt.12:41; adverbially, Acts.4:17 20:9 24:4. 
  3. As adv., πλεῖον: before ἤ, Luke.9:13; with genitive comp., Matt.5:20; πλείω: with num., Matt.26:53. 
 Superl., πλεῖστος, -η, -ον
,  (a) prop., most: Matt.11:20 21:8; adverbially, τὸ π., 1 Cor.14:27; 
  (b) elative (M, Pr., 79), very great: ὄχλος π., Mark.4:1. 
 (AS)

G4119.d:
πλέον, see: πολύς.
  πολύς, πολλή, πολύ, 
 [in LXX chiefly for רַב and cognate forms ;] 
  1. as adj., much, many, great, of number, space, degree, value, time, etc.: ἀριθμός, Acts.11:21; ὄχλος, Mark.5:24; θερισμός, Matt.9:37; χόρτος, John.6:10; χρόνος, Matt.25:19; γογγυσμός, John.7:12; πόνος, Col.4:13; δόξα, Matt.24:30; σιγή, Acts.21:40; pl., προφῆται, Matt.13:17; ὄχλοι, Matt.4:25; δαιμόνια, Mark.1:34; δυνάμεις, Matt.7:22, 
  2. As subst., pl. masc, πολλοί, many (persons): Matt.7:22, Mark.2:2, al.; with genitive partit., Matt.3:7, Luke.1:16, al.; before ἐκ, John.7:31, Acts.17:12; with art., οἱ π., the many, Matt.24:12, Rom.12:5, 1 Cor.10:17, 33 2 Cor.2:17; opposite to ὁ εἶς (Lft., Notes, 291), Rom.5:15, 19; neut. pl., πολλά: Matt.13:3, Mark.5:26, al.; accusative with adverbial force, Mark.1:45, Rom.16:6 (Deiss., LAE, 317), 1 Cor.16:12, Jas.3:2, al.; neut. sing., πολύ: Luke.12:48; adverbially, Mark.12:27, al.; πολλοῦ (genitive pret.), Matt.26:9; with compar. (Bl., §44, 5), π. σπουδαιότερον, 2 Cor.8:22; πολλῷ πλείους, John.4:41. 
 Compar., πλείων
, neut., πλεῖον and πλέον (see WH, App., 151), pl., πλείονες, -ας, -α, contr., πλείους, -ω (cf. Mayser, 69), more, greater; 
  1. as adj.: John.15:2, Acts.18:2o, Heb.3:3; before παρά, Heb.11:4 (cf. Westc, in l. Was ΠΛΙΟΝΑ here a primitive error for ΗΔΙΟΝΑ ?); pi., Acts.13:31, al.; with genitive compar., Matt.21:36; with num. (ἤ of comp. omitted), Acts.4:22 24:11, al. 
  2. As subst., οἱ π., the greater number: Acts.10:32 27:12, 1 Cor.10:5 15:6; also (Bl., §44, 3) others, more, the more: 2 Cor.2:6 4:15, Phil.1:14; πλείονα, Luke.11:53; πλειον, πλέον, Matt.20:10, 2 Tim.3:9; with genitive comp., Mk  12:43, Luke.21:3; π. Ἰωνᾶ ὧδε, Matt.12:41; adverbially, Acts.4:17 20:9 24:4. 
  3. As adv., πλεῖον: before ἤ, Luke.9:13; with genitive comp., Matt.5:20; πλείω: with num., Matt.26:53. 
 Superl., πλεῖστος, -η, -ον
,  (a) prop., most: Matt.11:20 21:8; adverbially, τὸ π., 1 Cor.14:27; 
  (b) elative (M, Pr., 79), very great: ὄχλος π., Mark.4:1. 
 (AS)

G4120.d:
πλέκω 
 [in LXX: Exod.28:14 (עֲבֹת), Isa.28:5 (צְפִירָה)* ;] 
to plait, twist, weave: Matt.27:29, Mark.15:17, John.19:2.†
 (AS)

G4121.d:
πλεονάζω
 (πλέον), [in LXX for עֲדַף, רָבָה, etc. ;] 
  I. Intrans. 
  1. Of persons; 
  (a) to abound in (Arist.); 
  (b) to superabound: 2 Cor.8:15 (LXX). 
  2. Of things, to abound, superabound: Rom.5:20 6:1, 2 Cor.4:15, Phil.4:17, 2 Thess.1:3, 2 Pet.1:8. 
  II. Trans. (Num.26:54, Ps.71:21; not cl, see Lft., Notes, 48 f.), to make to abound: 1 Thess.3:12 (cf. ὑπερ-πλεονάζω).†
 SYN.: περισσεύω, q.v  (AS)

G4122.d:
πλεονεκτέω, -ῶ
 (πλεονέκτης, which see), [in LXX: Hab.2:9, Eze.22:27 (בָּצַע), Jdg.4:11 B* ;] 
  1. intrans., to have more, to have an advantage (cl., with genitive of person(s)). 
  2. Trans., in late writers (see M, Pr., 65), to over­reach, defraud: with accusative of person(s), 2 Cor.7:2 12:17-18; ἐν τ. πράγματιι, 1 Thess.4:6 (see M, Th., in l); pass., 2 Cor.2:11 (as also in cl.; see LS, see word).†
 (AS)

G4123.d:
πλεονέκτης, -ου, ὁ
 (πλέον, ἔχω), [in LXX: Sir.14:9 * ;] 
= ὁ θέλων πλέον ἔχειν (see MM, xx), 
 one desirous of having more, covetous: 1 Cor.5:10-11 6:10 Eph.5:5.†
 (AS)

G4124.d:
πλεονεξία, -ας, ἡ
 (πλεονέκτης), [in LXX for בֶּצַע ;] 
the character and conduct of a πλεονέκτης. 
  1. advantage. 
  2. desire for advantage, grasping, aggression, cupidity, covetousness: Luke.12:15, Rom.1:29, 2 Cor.9:5, Eph.4:19 (see ICC, in l) Eph.5:3, Col.3:5, 1 Thess.2:5, 2 Pet.2:3 2:14; pl. (see Bl., § 32, 6), Mark.7:22.†
 SYN.: φιλαργυρία, avarice (see Tr., Syn., § xxiv)  (AS)

G4125.d:
πλευρά, -ᾶς, ἡ 
 [in LXX (frequently pl. as in Hom.) chiefly for צֵלָע ;] 
the side: Matt.27:49 ([[WH]] R, mg.), John.19:34 20:20, 25 20:27 Acts.12:7.†
 (AS)

G4126.d:
πλέω 
 [in LXX, before εἰς, Jon.1.3 (בּוֹא), I Est.4:23, Isa.42:10; before ἐπί, 4Ma.7:3; with accusative (poët.), Sir.43:24, 1Ma.13:29 (cf. Acts.27:2, Rec.) * ;] 
to sail: Luke.8:23, Acts.27:24; before εἰς, Acts.21:3 27:2, 6; ἐπί, Rev.18:17 
 (cf. ἀπό-, δια-, ἐκ-, κατα-, παρα-, ὑπο-πλέω).†
 (AS)

G4127.d:
πληγή, ῆς, ἡ
 (πλήσσω), [in LXX chiefly for מַכָּה, also for מַגֵּפָה etc. ;] 
  1. a blow, stripe, wound: pl., Luke.10:30 12:48, Acts.16:23, 33, 2 Cor.6:5 11:23; ἡ π. τ. θανάτου (RV, death-stroke), Rev.13:3, 12; τ. μαχαίρας, Rev.13:14. 
  2. Metaphorical, a calamity, plague: Rev.9:18, 20 11:6 15:1, 6 15:8 16:9, 21 18:4, 8 21:9 22:18.†
 (AS)

G4128.d:
πλῆθος, -ους, τό 
 [in LXX chiefly for רֹב, also for הָמוֹן, etc. ;] 
  1. a great number, a multitude; 
  (a) of things : ἰχθύων, Luke.5:6, John.21:6; φρυγάνων, Acts.28:3; ἁμαρτιίῶν, Jas.5:20, 1 Pet.4:8; τ. πλήθει, in multitude, Heb.11:12; 
  (b) of persons: Acts.21:22 (WH, R, om.); with genitive, Luke.2:13, John.5:3, Acts.5:14; π. πολύ (πολὺ π.), Mark.3:7-8; id. with genitive, Luke.6:17 23:27, Acts.14:1 17:4 
  2. Of persons, with art., the whole number, the multitude (in Plat., Thuc., Xen., al., = δῆμος, the commons, or-opposite to δῆμος-the populace) : Acts.2:6 15:30 19:9 23:7; τ. λαοῦ, Acts.21:36; τ. πόλεως, Acts.14:4; πᾶν τὸ π., Acts.15:12; with genitive, Luke.1:10 8:37 19:37 23:1, Acts.4:32 5:16 6:2, 5 25:24.†
 (AS)

G4129.d:
πληθύνω
 (causal of πληθύω, to be full, πληθύς, Ion. for πλῆθος),  [in LXX chiefly for רָבָה hi. ;] 
  1. trans., to increase, multiply: 2 Cor.9:10 6:14" (LXX) ; pass., to be increased, to multiply: Matt.24:12, Acts.6:7 7:17 9:31 12:24; with dative of person(s) (Dan LXX TH 3:31(98) al.), 1 Pet.1:2, 2 Pet.1:2, Ju 2. 
  2. Intrans., to be increased, to multiply: Acts.6:1.†
 (AS)

G4130.d:
πίμπλημι 
 [in LXX chiefly for מָלֵא, also for שָׂבַע ;] 
trans. form in present and imperfect of πλήθω (intrans. in these tenses), which supplies the other tense forms; 
 to fill: with accusative, Luke.5:7; with accusative and genitive, Matt.27:48; pass., Matt.22:10, Acts.19:29; of that which fills or takes possession of the mind : pass., with genitive, Luke.1:15, 41 1:67 4:28 5:26 6:11, Acts.2:4 3:10 4:8, 31 5:17 9:17 13:9, 45. Metaphorical (as in LXX for מָלֵא: Gen.29:27, Job.15:32), to complete, fulfil: pass., of prophecy, Luke.21:22; of time, Luke.1:23, 57 2:6, 21-22 (cf. ἐμ-πίμπλημι).†
 πλήθω, see: πίμπλημι 
 SYN.: πληροφορέω, πληρόω  (AS)

G4131.d:
πλήκτης, -ου, ὁ
 (πλήσσω), [in Sm.: Ps.35:15 * ;] 
a striker, brawler: 1 Tim.3:3, Titus.1:7 (Arist., Plut., al.).†
 (AS)

G4132.d:
πλήμμυρα, -ης (for Att.. -ας, see Bl., § 7, 1) 
 (πλήθω), [in LXX: π. γένεσθαι, Job.40:18 (23) (נָהָר עָשַׁק) * ;] 
a flood (of sea or river) : Luke.6:48.†
 (AS)

G4133.d:
πλήν 
 adv., [in LXX for רַק, בַּד, אַךְ, etc. ;] 
  1. introducing a clause (= ἀλλά, δέ; "it is obvious that πλήν was the regular word in the vulgar language": Bl., § 77, 13), yet, howbeit, only: Matt.11:22, 24 18:7 26:39, 64 (M, Pr., 86), Luke.6:24, 35 10:11, 14 10:20 11:41 12:31 13:33 17:1 18:8 19:27 22:21-22, 42 (WH, mg. om.) Luke.23:28, 1 Cor.11:11, Eph.5:33, Phil.3:16 4:14, Rev.2:25; π. ὅτι (Hdt., Plat., al.), except that, save that, Acts.20:23, Phil.1:18. 
  2. As prep., with genitive, except, save (cl.) : Mark.12:32, John.8:10, Acts.8:1 15:28 27:22.†
 (AS)

G4134.d:
πλήρης, -ες 
 [in LXX chiefly for מָלֵא ;] 
  1. full, filled: Matt.14:20 15:37; with genitive of thing(s), Mark.8:19; λέπρας, Luke.5:12; metaphorically, of the soul: πνεύματος ἀγίου, Luke.4:1, Acts.6:3 7:55 11:24; πίστεως, Acts.6:5; χάριτος, ib. Acts.6:8; χ. καὶ ἀληθείας (where π. is indecl.; see M, Pr., 50; Milligan, NTD, 65, with reff. in each), John.1:14; δόλου, Acts.13:10; θυμοῦ, Acts.19:28; ἔργων ἀγαθῶν, Acts.9:36. 
  2. full, complete: μισθός, II Jn 8; σῖτος (π. prob. in­decl. here; see on John.1:14, supr.), Mark.4:28.†
 (AS)

G4135.d:
πληροφορέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: Ecc.8:11 (מָלֵא) * ;] 
  1. to bring in full measure, hence, to fulfil, accomplish: Luke.1:1, 2 Tim.4:5 4:17. 
  2. to persuade, assure or satisfy fully (so in π.; see Deiss., LAE, 82 f.; M, Th., 9): pass., Rom.4:21 14:5, Col.4:12 (see Lft., in l). 
  3. to fill: Rom.15:13, L, mg. (Cl. Ro., 1 Cor.5:4); metaphorically, pass., to be filled with, hence, fully bent on (Ec, l.with).†
 (AS)

G4136.d:
πληροφορία, -ας, ἡ
 (πληροφορέω), 
full assurance, confidence: 1 Thess.1:5; τ. συνέσεως, Col.2:2; τ. ἐλπίδος, Heb.6:11; πίστεως, Heb.10:22 (cf. Lft. on Col., l.with; M, Th., 9).†
 (AS)

G4138.d:
πλήρωμα, -τος, τό
 (πληρόω), [in LXX for מְלֹא ;] 
the result of the action involved in πληρόω (Lft., Col., 255 if.; AR, Eph., 255 ff.), hence, 
  1. in passive sense, that which has been completed, complement, plenitude, fullness (in Xen., Luc., Polyb., al., of a ship's crew or cargo, and by meton. of the ship itself) : John.1:16, Rom.11:12, 25 15:29, 1 Cor.10:26" (LXX) Eph.1:23 (AR, 42 ff.) Eph.3:19 (AR. 87 ff.) Eph.4:13, Col.1:19 2:9; of time, Gal.4:4, Eph.1:10; κοφίνων (σφυρίδων) πληρώματα, basketfuls, Mark.6:43 8:20. 
  2. In active sense (= πλήρωσις, as frequently in words of these formations, cf. κτίσις, and see MM, xx); 
  (a) that which fills up (but see Lft., l.with) : Matt.9:16, Mark.2:21; 
  (b) a filling up, completing, fulfilment: Rom.13:10.†
 (AS)

G4139.d:
πλησίος, -α, -ον
 (πέλας, near), 
near, close by, neighbouring. As adv., πλησίον = πέλας, near: with genitive, John.4:5; with art., ὁ π., one's neigh­bour 
 [in LXX chiefly for רֵעַ ]: 
 Luke.10:29, 36, Acts.7:27, Rom.13:10 15:2, Eph.4:25, Jas.4:12; ἀγαπήσεις τὸν π. σου ὡς σεαυτόν (Lev.19:18, LXX), Matt.5:43 19:19 22:39, Mark.12:31, 33, Luke.10:27, Rom.13:9, Gal.5:14, Jas.2:8 (on the various senses of ὁ π. in OT, NT, see DB, iii, 511; DCC, ii, 240 f.).†
 (AS)

G4140.d:
πλησμονή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (πίμπλημι), [in LXX chiefly for שָׂבֵעַ and cognate forms ;] 
a filling up, satiety: πρὸς π. σαρκός (RV, against the indulgence of the flesh; but ICC, in l, for the full satisfaction of the flesh, op. cit., 276 ff.), Col.2:23.†
 (AS)

G4141.d:
πλήσσω 
 [in LXX chiefly for נָכָה hi., ho. ;] 
to strike, smite: pass., Rev.8:12 (cf. ἐπι, πλήσσω).†
 (AS)

G4142.d:
πλοιάριον, -ου, τό
 (dimin. of πλοῖον), 
a boat: Mark.3:9, Luke.5:2 (πλοῖα, WH, txt., R), John.6:22-23 (πλοῖα, WH) John.6:24 21:8.†
 (AS)

G4143.d:
πλοῖον, -ον, τό
 (πλέω), [in LXX chiefly for אֳנִיָּה ;] 
a boat, also (= obsolete ναῦς) a ship: Matt.4:21-22, and frequently in Gosp. and Ac, Jas.3:4, Rev.8:9 18:19. 
 (AS)

G4144.d:
πλόος, πλούς genitive, -όου, -oῦ (and in late writers also πλοός, like νοός from νοῦς), ὁ 
 (πλέω), [in LXX: Wis.14:1 * ;] 
a voyage: Acts.21:7 27:9-10.†
 (AS)

G4145.d:
πλούσιος, -α, -ον
 (πλοῦτος), [in LXX chiefly for עָשִׁיר ;] 
rich, wealthy: Matt.27:57, Luke.12:16 14:12 16:1, 19 18:23 19:2. Substantively, ὁ π., Luke.16:21-22, Jas.1:10-11; oἱ π., Luke.6:24 21:1, 1 Tim.6:17, Jas.2:6 5:1, Rev.6:15 13:16; anarth., a rich man, Matt.19:23-24, Mark.10:25 12:41, Luke.18:25. Metaphorical, of God, ἐν ἐλέει (= cl., with genitive, dative), Eph.2:4; of Christ, 2 Cor.8:9; of Christians, Rev.2:9 3:17; ἐν πίστει, Jas.2:5.†
 (AS)

G4146.d:
πλουσίως 
 adv., 
richly, abundantly: Col.3:16, 1 Tim.6:17. Titus.3:6, 2 Pet.1:11.†
 (AS)

G4147.d:
πλουτέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX chiefly for עָשַׁר hi. ;] 
to be rich, aor., to become rich: Luke.1:53, 1 Tim.6:9; before ἀπό (Sir.11:18), Rev.18:15; ἐκ, Rev.18:3, 19; ἐν (= cl., with genitive, dative, accusative, cf. πλούσιος), 1 Tim.6:18. Metaphorical, π. εἰς θεόν, Luke.12:21; of God, εἰς πάντας, Rom.10:12; aor., I became rich, 1 Cor.4:8, 2 Cor.8:9, Rev.3:18; pf., I have become rich, Rev.3:17.†
 (AS)

G4148.d:
πλουτίζω
 (πλοῦτος), [in LXX chiefly for עָשַׁר hi. ;] 
to make rich, enrich: with accusative of person(s), pass., 2 Cor.9:11. Metaphorical, of spiritual riches, with accusative: of person(s), 2 Cor.6:10; before ἐν, pass., 1 Cor.1:5.†
 (AS)

G4149.d:
πλοῦτος, -ου, ὁ and (in 2 Cor.8:2, Eph.1:17 2:7 3:8, 16, Phil.4:19, Col.1:27 2:2; see WH, App., 158; M, Pr., 60) τό, 
 [in LXX chiefly for עֹשֶׁר ;] 
riches, wealth: of external possessions, Matt.13:22, Mark.4:19, Luke.8:14, 1 Tim.6:17, Jas.5:2, Rev.18:16; of moral and spiritual conceptions, Rom.2:4 9:23 11:12, 33, 2 Cor.8:2, Eph.1:7, 18 2:7 3:8, 16 Phil.4:19, Col.1:27 2:2, Heb.11:26, Rev.5:12.†
 (AS)

G4150.d:
πλύνω 
 [in LXX chiefly for כָּבַס pi. ;] 
to wash (inanimate objects, esp. clothing): τ. δίκτυα, Luke.5:2. Fig., τ. στολάς, Rev.7:14 22:14 (cf. Ps.51:4, 9 and see: ἀπο-πλύνω).†
 SYN.: see: λούω  (AS)

G4151.d:
πνεῦμα, -τος, τό, 
 [in LXX chiefly and very frequently for רוּחַ ;] 
  1. of air in motion; 
  (a) wind: John.3:8; pl., Heb.1:7 (LXX); 
  (b) breath: π. ζωῆς, Rev.11:11; π. τοῦ στόματος, figuratively, 2 Thess.2:8 (cf. Ps 32 (33)6). 
  2. (always in LXX and NT), ־ομαι, to go, proceed, go on one's way: with accusative, ὁδόν, Acts.8:39; before ἐκεῖθεν, Matt.19:15; ἐντεῦθεν, Luke.13:31; ἀπό, Matt.25:41, Luke.4:42; εἰς, Matt.2:20, Mark.16:12, Luke.1:39, John.7:35, al; εἰς εἰρήνην (cf. 1Ki.1:17).  (AS)

G4199.d:
πορθέω  collat. form (in cl. chiefly poët.) of πέρθω, 
 [in LXX: 4Ma.4:23 4Mac 11:4 * ;]

πορισμός, -ου, ὁ

 (AS)

G4201.d:
Πόρκιος, -ου, ὁ 
 Porcius, prænomen of Porcius Festus (see: Φῆστος): Acts.24:27.†
 (AS)

G4202.d:
πορνεία, -ας, ἡ
 (πορνεύω), [in LXX for תַּזְנוּת and cogn. forms ;] 
fornication: Acts.15:20, 29 21:25, 1 Cor.5:1 6:13 6:18, 2 Cor.12:21, Gal.5:19, Eph.5:3, Col.3:5, 1 Thess.4:3 (Lft., Notes, 53), Rev.9:21; pl. (see WM, 220; Bl., § 32, 6), 1 Cor.7:2; disting. from μοιχεία, Matt.15:19, Mark.7:21; = μοιχεία (Amos 8:17 Sir.23:23, al.), Matt.5:32 19:9.  (AS)

G4203.d:
πορνεύω 
 [in LXX for זָנָה ;] 
  1. to prostitute the body for hire. 
  2. to commit fornication: Mark.10:19 (WH, mg), 1 Cor.6:18 10:8, Rev.2:14, 20. Metaphorical (as in LXX: 1Ch.5:25, Jer.3:6, Hos.9:1, al.), of idolatry (but see Swete, Ap., 180 f.), Rev.17:2 18:3, 9 (cf. ἐκ- πορνεύω).†
 (AS)

G4204.d:
πόρνη, -ης, ἡ 
 [in LXX chiefly for זָנָה ;] 
a prostitute, harlot: Matt.21:31-32, Luke.15:30, 1 Cor.6:15-16 Heb.11:31, Jas.2:25. Metaphorical (see Swete, Ap., 180 f.), of Babylon (i.e. Rome): Rev.17:1, 5 17:15-16 19:2.†
 (AS)

G4205.d:
πόρνος, -ου, ὁ 
 [in LXX: Sir.23:16-18 * ;]

  2. a fornicator: 1 Cor.5:9-11 6:9, Eph.5:5, 1 Tim.1:10, Heb.12:15 13:4, Rev.21:8 22:15.†

G4206.d:
πόρρω

G4207.d:
πόρρωθεν 
 adv. (τόρρω, which see), [in LXX for רָחוֹק and cogn. forms ;]

 (AS)

G4209.d:
πορφύρα, -ας, ἡ 
 [in LXX for אַרְגָּמָן, אַרְגְּוָן ;] 
  1. the purple fish (cf. 1Ma.4:23).

G4210.d:
πορφύρεος, -α, -ον contr., -οῦς, -ᾶ, -οῦν

 (AS)

G4211.d:
πορφυρόπωλις, -ιδος, ἡ 
 a seller of purple fabrics: Acts.16:14.†
 (AS)

G4212.d:
ποσάκις

 how often: Matt.18:21 23:37, Luke.13:34.†
 (AS)

G4213.d:
πόσις, -εως, ἡ
 (πίνω), [in LXX: Da, LXX TH Dan.1:10 (מִשְׁתֶּה) * ;] 
  1. prop., drinking: Rom.14:17, Col.2:16 (see Lft.; ICC, in l).

πόσος, -η, -ον

G4215.d:
ποταμός, -οῦ, ὁ 
 [in LXX chiefly for נָהָר, יְאֹר ;]

πότε

G4220.d:
πότερος, -α, -ον 
 which of two. Neut., adverbially, πότερον, whether: John.7:17.†
 (AS)

G4221.d:
ποτήριον, -ου, τό dimin. of ποτήρ 
 (πίνω), [in LXX chiefly for כּוֹס:] 
a wine cup: Matt.23:25-26 26:27, Mark.7:4 14:23, Luke.11:39 22:17, 20 a (WH, R, mg., cm.), 1 Cor.11:25, Rev.17:4; πίνειν ἐκ τοῦ π., 1 Cor.11:28; with genitive of thing(s), Matt.10:42, Mark.9:41; τ. εὐλογίας, 1 Cor.10:16; by meton., of the contents of the cup, Luke.22:20 b (WH, R, mg., cm.), 1 Cor.11:25-26; with genitive of person(s), 1 Cor.10:21 11:27. G4239.d:
πραΰς, -εῖα, -ΰ, and πρᾷος
 (Or πρᾶος, ν. Bl., § 3, 3), -α, -ον (see LS, Thayer, see word), [in LXX (always -ΰς, exc. 2Ma.15:12, -ᾷος, see Thackeray, Gr., 180 f.) for עָנָו, עָנִי ;] 
gentle, meek: Matt.5:5 11:29 21:5" (LXX) 1 Pet.3:4.†

G4240.d:
πραΰτης
 (Rec. -ότης, exc. Ja, 1Pe, ll. with, where πρᾳύτης), -ητος, ἡ,  late form of πραότης, [in LXX: Ps.45:4 90:10 132:1 (עַנְוָה, עֱנוּת, Est.5:1, Sir.6:1-37 * ;]

 SIN.: ἐπιεικία, q.v 
 (AS)

πρέπω 
 [in LXX: Ps.93:5 (נָאָה pi.), etc. ;] 
  1. to be clearly seen. 
  2. to resemble. 
  3. to be fitting or becoming, to suit: with dative, Heb.7:26, 1 Tim.2:10, Titus.2:1; impers., with dative, Eph.5:3; id. before inf., Heb.2:10; πρέπον ἐστίν, with dative of person(s) and inf., Matt.3:15; with accusative and inf., 1 Cor.11:13 (see Bl., § 72, 5).†

G4242.d:
πρεσβεία, -ας, ἡ
 (πρεσβεύω), [in LXX: 2Ma.4:11 * ;]

  3. an embassy; by meton., of the am­bassadors, embassy: Luke.14:32 19:14.†

πρεσβεύω
 (πρέσβυς),

πρεσβυτέριον, -ου, τό

 (AS)

G4246.d:
πρεσβύτης, -ου prose form of πρέσβυς, which see, 
 [in LXX chiefly for זָקֵן, Gen.25:8, al.; also (= πρεσβευτής), 2Ch.32:31 Bl (לוּץ), 1Ma.14:22 S, al. (see Thackeray, Gr., 97) ;] 
  1. an old man: Luke.1:18, Titus.2:2, Phm 9 (R, txt., but see infr.). 
  2. As in LXX, also = πρεσβευτής, an am­bassador: Phm 9 (R, mg., see Lft. and ICC, in l).†
 (AS)

G4247.d:
πρεσβῦτις, -ιδος, ἡ fem, of πρεσβύτης, 
 [in LXX: 4Ma.16:14 * ;] 
an aged woman: Titus.2:3.†
 (AS)

G4248.d:
πρηνής, -ές
 (in Att.. also πρανής), [in LXX: Wis.4:19, 3Ma.5:43 3Mac 5:50 3Mac 6:23 * ;] 
headlong, prone: Acts.1:18.†
 (AS)

G4249.d:
πρίζω = πρίω, 
 [in LXX: Amo.1:3, Da TH Su 1:59 * ;] 
to saw, saw asunder (= π. δίχα, Thuc., iv, 100): pass, Heb.11:37 (cf. δια-πρίω).†
 (AS)

G4251.d:
Πρίσκα, -ας, ἡ (Lat.), and Πρίσκιλλα, -ης, ἡ, Prisca: Rom_16:3, 1Co_16:19, 2Ti_4:19; Priscilla: Act_18:2; Act_18:18; Act_18:26; the wife of Aquila, vs. Ἀκύλας.†
 (AS)

G4252.d:
Πρίσκιλλα, see: Πρίσκα.
  Πρίσκα, -ας, ἡ (Lat.), and Πρίσκιλλα, -ης, ἡ, Prisca: Rom_16:3, 1Co_16:19, 2Ti_4:19; Priscilla: Act_18:2; Act_18:18; Act_18:26; the wife of Aquila, vs. Ἀκύλας.†
 (AS)

G4254.d:
προ-άγω 
 [in LXX: 1Ki.17:16 (נָגַשׁ), Wis.19:11, al. ;] 
  1. prop. trans., to lead on, lead forth or forward: with accusative of person(s), Acts.16:30 17:5; of bringing forth to trial, Acts.12:6 (WH, txt., προσάγ-); before ἐπί, with genitive of person(s), Acts.25:26. 
  2. Intrans. (Plat., Polyb., and later writers; see Bl., § 53, 1; MM, xxi); 
  (a) to lead the way, 1 Tim.1:18 (R, mg.), hence, to go before, precede: Luke.18:39; opposite to ἀκολουθέω, Mark.11:9; before εἰς, Matt.14:22, Mark.6:45, 1 Tim.5:24, Heb.7:18; with accusative of person(s), Matt.2:9 21:9, Mark.10:32; before εἰς, Matt.21:31 26:32 28:7, Mark.14:28 16:7; 
  (b) to go on, advance (Sir.20:27): 2 John.9.†
 (AS)

G4255.d:
προ-αιρέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: for חָשַׁק, etc. ;] 
to bring forth or forward. Most frequently in mid., to take by choice, prefer, propose: 2 Cor.9:7.†
 (AS)

G4256.d:
προ-αιτιάομαι, -ῶμαι 
 to accuse or charge beforehand: Rom.3:9 (not elsewhere) .†
 (AS)

G4257.d:
προ-ακούω 
 to hear beforehand: Col.1:5 (see Lft., in l).†
 (AS)

G4259.d:
προ-αύλιον, -ου, τό
 (πρό, αὐλή), 
a porch, vestibule: Mark.14:68.†
 (AS)

G4260.d:
προ-βαίνω 
 [in LXX chiefly for בּוֹא ;] 
to go forwards, go on, advance: Matt.4:21, Mark.1:19. Metaphorical, of age (Gen.18:11, al., Lys., Diod., al.), ἐν τ. ἡμέραις, Luke.1:7, 18 2:36.†
 (AS)

G4261.d:
προ-βάλλω 
 [in LXX for חוּד, מָרַק, etc. ;] 
  1. to throw before. 
  2. to put forward: with accusative, Acts.19:33; of trees, to put forth, produce (sc. φύλλα), Luke.21:30.†
 (AS)

G4262.d:
προβατικός, -ή, -όν
 (πρόβατον) [in LXX (π. πύλη): Neh.3:1, 32 12:39 (צֹאן)* ;] 
of sheep: ἡ π. (sc. πύλη, see supr.), the sheep-gate, John.5:2.†
 (AS)

G4263.d:
πρόβατον, -ου, τό
 (προβαίνω), [in LXX chiefly for צֹאן, also for שֶׂה, more rarely for כֶּבֶשׂ (כֶּשֶׂב), רָחֵל ;] 
  1. in Hom., Hdt., cattle, esp. of small cattle, sheep and goats. 
  2. In NT, as in Attic writers generally (cf. MM, xxi), a sheep: Matt.7:15, Mark.6:34, al.; πρόβατα σφαγῆς, Rom.8:36 (LXX). Metaphorical (in cl. of timidity, stupidity or idleness), of the followers of a leader or master, esp. of those who are subject to the care of the Good Shepherd: Matt.10:6 15:24 26:31" (LXX) Mark.14:27 (LXX), John.10:7-8, 15-16 10:26-27 21:16-17 (WH txt., προβάτια), Heb.13:20; opposite to ἐρίφια, Matt.25:33. 
 προβάτιον, -ου, τό, 
 dimin. of πρόβατον (used as a term of endearment, see El., § 27, 4), a little sheep: John.21:16-17 (πρόβατα, WH, mg.).†
 (AS)

G4264.d:
προ-βιβάζω  causal of προβαίνω, 
 [in LXX: Exod.35:34 (יָרָה hi.), Deu.6:7 (שָׁנַן pi.) * ;] 
to lead forward, lead on; metaphorically, to induce, incite, urge: Matt.14:8.†
 (AS)

G4265.d:
προ-βλέπω 
 [in LXX: Ps.37:13 (רָאָה)* ;] 
to foresee: mid., Heb.11:40 (see Bl., § 24, 55, 1).†
 (AS)

G4266.d:
προ-γίνομαι 
 [in LXX: Wis.19:13 אA, 2Ma.14:3 2Mac 15:8 * ;] 
to happen before: pf. pass. ptcp., Rom.3:25.†
 (AS)

G4267.d:
προ-γινώσκω 
 [in LXX: Wis.6:13 8:8 18:6 * ;] 
to know beforehand, foreknow: 2 Pet.3:17; with accusative of person(s), Acts.26:5; of the Divine foreknowledge, Rom.8:29 11:2, 1 Pet.1:20.†
 (AS)

G4268.d:
πρό-γνωσις, -εως, ἡ
 (προγινώσκω) [in LXX: Jdth.9:6 11:19 * ;] 
fore­knowledge: Acts.2:23, 1 Pet.1:2.†
 (AS)

G4269.d:
πρό-γονος, -ον
 (προγίνομαι), [in LXX: Est.4:17, Sir.8:4, al. ;] 
  1. born before. 
  2. As subst., in pl., οἱ π., ancestors, forefathers: 2 Tim.1:3; of living parents (so Plat.), 1 Tim.5:4.†
 (AS)

G4270.d:
προ-γράφω 
 [in LXX: Dan LXX 3:3 cod., 1Ma.10:36 * ;] 
  1. to write before: Rom.15:4, Eph.3:3, Ju 4. 
  2. to write in public, placard, proclaim (Dem., Plut., al.): Gal.3:1 (Lft., in l). 
  3. = ζωγραφέω, to pourtray, depict: Ga, l.with (Syr. Pesh., Chrys.; Field, Notes, 189; CGT, in l).†
 (AS)

G4271.d:
πρό-δηλος, -ον 
 [in LXX: Jdth.8:29, 2Ma.3:17 2Mac 14:39 * ;] 
  1. evident beforehand. 
  2. clearly evident: 1 Tim.5:24-25 Heb.7:14.†
 (AS)

G4272.d:
προ-δίδωμι 
 [in LXX: Eze.16:34 A (נָתַן), 4Ma.4:1, al. ;] 
  1. to give before, give first: Rom.11:35 (Job.41:2 (11) LXX, al.). 
  2. to betray (4Mac, l.with).†
 (AS)

G4273.d:
προ-δότης, -ου, ὁ
 (προδίδωμι) [in LXX: 2Ma.5:15 2Mac 10:13 2Mac 10:22, 3Ma.3:24 * ;] 
a betrayer, traitor: Luke.6:16, Acts.7:52, 2 Tim.3:4.†
 (AS)

G4274.d:
πρό-δρομος, -ον
 (προτρέχω) [in LXX: Num.13:21 (20), Isa.28:4 (בִּכּוּר),  Wis.12:8 * ;] 
running forward, going in advance. As subst., ὁ π., an advance guard, forerunner: Heb.6:20.†
 (AS)

G4275.d:
προ-εῖδον  aor. without Pres. in use (see: προοράω), 
 [in LXX: Gen.37:18 (רָאָה), Ps.139:3 (סָכַן hi.) * ;] 
to foresee: Acts.2:31 (προϊδών; WH, προιδών), Gal.3:8.†
 (AS)

G4276.d:
προ-ελπίζω 
 to hope before: before ἐν, Eph.1:12.†
 (AS)

G4277.d:
προ-εῖπον  2 aor. from unused Pres. (see: εἶπον, and pf., -είρηκα (3Ma.6:35 *), pass., -είρημαι (2Ma.2:32, 3Ma.1:26, al.), 
  1. to say before: Gal.1:9, 1 Thess.4:6 (on the form -αμεν, see WH, App., 164), Heb.4:7; before ὅτι, 2 Cor.7:3 13:2, Gal.5:21; of prophecy, Matt.24:25, Mark.13:23, Acts.1:16, Rom.9:29, 2 Pet.3:2, Ju 17. 
  2. to proclaim publicly, declare openly or plainly (cl.): so R, mg., in 2 Cor.13:2, Gal.5:21, 1 Thess.4:6 (cf. προλέγω; but see supr., and cf. M, Th., 38).†
 (AS)

G4278.d:
προ-ενάρχομαι 
 to begin before: 2 Cor.8:6; with accusative, τὸ θέλειν, 2 Cor.8:10 (not elsewhere).†
 (AS)

G4279.d:
προ-επ-αγγέλλω 
 to announce before. Mid., to promise before: with accusative of thing(s), Rom.1:2, 2 Cor.9:5 (Dio. Cass.).†
 (AS)

G4280.d:
προ-ερέω, -ῶ, see: προεῖπον.
  προ-εῖπον  2 aor. from unused Pres. (see: εἶπον, and pf., -είρηκα (3Ma.6:35 *), pass., -είρημαι (2Ma.2:32, 3Ma.1:26, al.), 
  1. to say before: Gal.1:9, 1 Thess.4:6 (on the form -αμεν, see WH, App., 164), Heb.4:7; before ὅτι, 2 Cor.7:3 13:2, Gal.5:21; of prophecy, Matt.24:25, Mark.13:23, Acts.1:16, Rom.9:29, 2 Pet.3:2, Ju 17. 
  2. to proclaim publicly, declare openly or plainly (cl.): so R, mg., in 2 Cor.13:2, Gal.5:21, 1 Thess.4:6 (cf. προλέγω; but see supr., and cf. M, Th., 38).†
 (AS)

G4281.d:
προ-έρχομαι 
 [in LXX: Gen.33:3, 14 R (עָבַר), Jdth.2:19, Sir.35:10 (Sir.32:10) al ;] 
  1. to go forward, go on, advance: before μικρόν, Matt.26:39 and Mark.14:35 (WH, mg., προσελθών): ῥύμην μίαν (cf. Plat., Rep., i, 328e), Acts.12:10. 
  2. Of relative position, to go before, precede: with genitive (cl.; Jth, l.with); with accusative of person(s) (not cl.), Luke.22:47 (with genitive, Rec.); before ἐνώπιον, Luke.1:17 (cf. Gen.33:3). 
  3. Of time, to go before or in advance: Acts.20:5, 13 (WH, mg., R, mg.), 2 Cor.9:5; with accusative of person(s) (= cl. φθάνω), Mark.6:33.†
 (AS)

G4282.d:
προ-ετοιμάζω 
 [in LXX: Isa.28:24 B, Wis.9:8 * ;] 
to prepare before: with accusative of thing(s), Rom.9:23 (οἱς for ἅ by attraction), Eph.2:10.†
 (AS)

G4283.d:
προ-ευαγγελίζομαι 
 to announce glad tidings beforehand: Gal.3:8.†
 (AS)

G4284.d:
προ-έχω 
 [in LXX: Job.27:6 A (חָזַק hi.) * ;] 
  1. Trans., to hold before; mid., to hold something before oneself (Hdt.), hence, metaphorically, to excuse oneself: Rom.3:9, R, mg. (but see Field, Notes, 152 f.; Lft., Notes, 266 f.; ICC and Vau., in l). 
  2. Intrans. 
  (a) to project; 
  (b) in running, to have the start, hence, metaphorically, to excel: pass., Ro, l.with, R, txt. (see reff. supr.).†
 (AS)

G4285.d:
προ-ηγέσμαι 
 [in LXX: Deu.20:9 (בְּרוֹשׁ), Pro.17:14 (פָּנִים), 2Ma.4:40, al. ;] 
  1. to go before as leader (in cl., with genitive, dative): Rom.12:10 (Chrys., Vg., al.; see ICC, in l). 
  2. In a sense not elsewhere found, ἀλλήλους προηγούμενοι = ἀ. ἡγούμενοι ὑπερέχοντας: Ro, l.with (ICC, cf. 1 Thess.5:13, Phil.2:3 and EV "preferring").†
 (AS)

G4286.d:
πρό-θεσις, -εως, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Exod.40:4, 23 (עֵרֶךְ), 1Ch.9:32, al. (מַעֲרֶכֶת), 2Ch.4:19 (פָּנִים), 1Ma.1:22, 2Ma.3:8, al. ;] 
  1. a setting forth (Plat., Plut., al.): οἱ ἄρτοι τῆς π. (cf. LXX, ll. with, elsewhere ἄρτοι ἐνώπιοι, Exod.25:29; οἱ ἄ. τοῦ προσώπου, Neh.10:33), Matt.12:4, Mark.2:26, Luke.6:4; ἡ π. τῶν ἄρτων, Heb.9:2. 
  2. a purpose (Mist., Polyb., al.; 2Mac, l.with): Acts.11:23 27:13, Rom.8:28 9:11, Eph.1:11 3:11, 2 Tim.1:9 3:10.†
 (AS)

G4287.d:
προ-θέσμιος, -α, -ον 
 [in Sm.: Job.28:3, Dan.9:26 * ;] 
appointed before­hand. In Attic law, as subst. (so always in cl.), ἡ π. (sc. ἡμέρα), a day appointed beforehand, a previously appointed time: Gal.4:2.†
 (AS)

G4288.d:
προθυμία, -ας, ἡ
 (πρόθυμος), [in LXX: Sir.45:23 * ;] 
eagerness, willingness, readiness: Acts.17:11, 2 Cor.8:11-12 8:19 9:2.†
 (AS)

G4289.d:
πρόθυμος, -ον 
 [in LXX: 1Ch.28:21, 2Ch.29:31 (נָדִיב), Hab.1:8 (חוּשׁ), al. ;] 
willing, ready: Matt.26:41, Mark.14:38; neut., τὸ π. = ἡ προθυμία (Thuc., al., 3Ma.5:26), οὕτως τὸ κατ᾽ ἐμὲ (= cl. τὸ ἐμὸν) π., Rom.1:15 (but see ICC, in l).†
 (AS)

G4290.d:
προθύμως 
 [in LXX: 2Ch.29:34 (יָשָׁר לֵבָב), Tob.7:8, al. ;] 
eagerly, readily, with a ready mind: 1 Pet.5:2.†
 (AS)

G4291.d:
προ-ΐστημι 
 [in LXX: 2Ki.13:17, Pro.23:5 26:17, Isa.43:24, Amo.6:10 (no proper Heb. equiv.), Dan LXX Bel 1:7, 1Ma.5:19, 4Ma.11:27 * ;] 
  1. trans. in fut., 1 aor., and mid. 1 aor., to put before, set over (Plat., al.). 
  2. Intrans., in pf., plpf., 2 aor. and mid. Pres. and impf.; 
  (a) to preside, rule, govern: Rom.12:8, 1 Tim.5:17; with genitive, 1 Thess.5:12, 1 Tim.3:4-5 3:12; 
  (b) to direct, maintain: with genitive of thing(s), καλῶν ἔργων, Titus.3:8, 14 (on R, mg., profess honest occupations, see CGT, in l; Field, Notes, 223 f.).†
 (AS)

G4292.d:
προ-καλέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: 2Ma.8:11 A * ;] 
to call forth. 
 Most frequently in mid., 
  (a) to challenge; hence, to provoke: Gal.5:26; 
  (b) to invite (2Mac, l.with).†
 (AS)

G4293.d:
προ-κατ-αγγέλλω 
 to announce beforehand: with accusative and inf., Acts.3:18; before περί, Acts.7:52.†
 (AS)

G4294.d:
προ-κατ-αρτίζω 
 to make ready beforehand: 2 Cor.9:5.†
 (AS)

G4295.d:
πρό-κειμαι 
 [in LXX: Exod.39:18 (36), Num.4:7 (פָּנִים), etc. ;] 
used as pass. of προτίθημι; 
  1. to be set before one, to be set forth: Heb.6:18 12:1-2, Ju 7. 
  2. to present oneself, be present: 2 Cor.8:12 (see Mey., in l).†
 (AS)

G4296.d:
προ-κηρύσσω 
  1. to proclaim by herald. 
  2. Of one who acts as a herald, to proclaim: Acts.13:24.†
 (AS)

G4297.d:
προ-κοπή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (προκόπτω), [in LXX: Sir.51:17, 2Ma.8:8 * ;] 
progress (prop., on a journey, then generally): Phil.1:12, 25, 1 Tim.4:15 (condemned by Atticists, see Rutherford, NPhr., 158).†
 (AS)

G4298.d:
προ-κόπτω 
 [in Sm.: Ps.45:5 * ;] 
to cut forward a way, for­ward, advance, in cl. trans. with neut. adj., as οὐδὲν π., τὰ πολλὰ π. In late writers (Polyb., al.), wholly intrans., to advance, progress: of time, Rom.13:12. Metaphorical, Luke.2:52, Gal.1:14, 2 Tim.2:16 3:9 3:13.†
 (AS)

G4299.d:
πρό-κριμα, -τος, τό
 (cl. προκρίνειν, 1. to prefer. 2. to judge beforehand), 
pre-judging, prejudice: 1 Tim.5:21 (see Cremer, 378).†
 (AS)

G4300.d:
προ-κυρόω, -ῶ 
 to establish or confirm beforehand: Gal.3:17.†
 (AS)

G4301.d:
προ-λαμβάνω 
 [in LXX: Wis.17:11 א2, Wis.17:17 א2B * ;] 
  1. to take beforehand: with accusative, 1 Cor.11:21 (but see infr.). 
  2. to be beforehand,  anticipate (in cl., with accusative, genitive or dative): with inf. (= cl. φθάνω, see Bl., § 69, 4; Swete, in l), Mark.14:8. 
  3. to overtake, surprise: pass., Gal.6:1 (on the virtual disappearance of the temporal force of the preposi­tion in this compound here and perhaps also in 1Co, l.with, see MM, xxi).†
 (AS)

G4302.d:
προ-λέγω 
 [in LXX: Isa.41:26 (נָגַד hi.) * ;] 
  1. to tell or say before­hand: 2 Cor.13:2, Gal.5:21, 1 Thess.3:4 (R, txt.; cf. προεῖπον, but see infr.). 
  2. to declare, tell plainly: 2Co, Ga, 1Th, ll. with (R, mg.; see MM, xxi, and cf. Isa, l.with).†
 (AS)

G4303.d:
προ-μαρτύρομαι 
 to protest beforehand (cf. μαρτύρομαι, and V. Hort, in l): 1 Pet.1:11 (elsewhere only in Theod. Met., xiv/AD.).†
 (AS)

G4304.d: to practise beforehand : with infinitive, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G4305.d:
προ-μεριμνάω, -ῶ 
 to be anxious beforehand: Mark.13:11.†
 (AS)

G4306.d:
προ-μοέω, -ῶ and depon. -έομαι, οῦμαι, 
 [in LXX: Dan LXX 11:37 (בִּין), Wis.6:7, al. ;] 
  1. to foresee. 
  2. to provide (RV, take thought for): with accusative of thing(s), καλά, Rom.12:17 (-ούμενοι), 2 Cor.8:21 (-οῦμεν). 
  3. to provide for (before περί, Wis, l.with): with genitive of person(s), 1 Tim.5:8 (-εῖ, WH, mg., -εῖται).†
 (AS)

G4307.d:
πρόνοια, -ας, ἡ
 (πρόνοος, careful) [in LXX: Dan LXX 6:18 (19) Wis.14:3 17:2, 4Mac.6:1-35 * ;] 
foresight, forethought: Acts.24:3; π. ποιεῖσθαι, with genitive (Dem., 546, 6), make provision for, show care for: Rom.13:14.†
 (AS)

G4308.d:
προ-οράω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: Ps.16:8) (שָׁוָה pi.), I Est.5:63 A * ;] 
to see before (as to place or time): with accusative, Acts.21:29. Mid., with accusative, before ἐνώπιόν μου, Acts.2:25 (LXX).†
 (AS)

G4309.d:
προ-ορίζω 
 to predetermine, foreordain: with accusative, Rom.8:30; id. and inf., Acts.4:28; id. before εἰς, 1 Cor.2:7, Eph.1:5; with dupl. accusative, Rom.8:26; pass., Eph.1:11.†
 (AS)

G4310.d: to suffer first  or beforehand , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: to be ill-treated before , ὑπό τινος (Thucydides):—;also, ἀγαθὸν πρ. (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G4311.d:
προ-πέμπω 
 [in LXX: I Est.4:47, Jdth.10:15, Wis.19:2, 1Ma.12:4, 2Ma.6:23 * ;] 
  1. to send before, send forth. 
  2. to set forward on a journey, escort: with accusative of person(s), 1 Cor.16:11, Titus.3:13, 3 John.6; before εἰς, Acts.20:38; οὗ, 1 Cor.16:6; ἕως, Acts.21:5; pass., Acts.15:3, Rom.15:24, 2 Cor.1:16.†
 (AS)

G4312.d:
προπετής, -ές
 (προπίπτω), [in LXX: Pro.10:14 (אֱוִיל) Pro.13:3 (פָּשַׂק) Sir.9:18 * ;] 
falling forwards, headlong. Metaphorical, precipitate, rash, reck­less: of persons, 2 Tim.3:4; of things, Acts.19:36.†
 (AS)

G4313.d:
προ-πορεύω 
 [in LXX chiefly for הָלַךְ, also for עָבַר, etc. ;] 
to make to go before. Pass. and mid., to go before: Luke.1:76, Acts.7:40" (LXX) ,†
 (AS)

G4315.d:
προ-σάββατον, -ου, τό 
 [in LXX: Ps.92:1-15 title. א (שַׁבָּת) שַׁבָּת) Ps.93:1-5 title., Jdth.8:6 * ;] 
the day before the Sabbath: Mark.15:42 (L, Tr., txt., πρὸς σ.).†
 (AS)

G4316.d:
προσ-αγορεύω 
 [in LXX: Deu.23:6 (7) (דָּרַשׁ), ?Est.10:11 (יָדָה hith.), Wis.14:22, 1Ma.14:40, 2Ma.1:36 2Mac 4:7 2Mac 10:9 2Mac 14:37 * ;] 
to address, greet, salute; hence, to call by name, address, style: with dupl. accusative, pass., Heb.5:10.†
 (AS)

G4317.d:
προσ-άγω 
 [in LXX chiefly for = קָרַב hi., also for נָגַשׁ etc. ;] 
  1. trans., to bring or lead: with accusative and dative, Acts.16:20; metaphorically, τ. θεῷ, 1 Pet.3:18; before ὧδε, Luke.9:41; pass., with dative, Matt.18:24 (προσηνέχθη, T); in forensic sense, to summon: Acts.12:6 (προαγαγεῖν, T, WH, mg., R). 
  2. Intrans., to draw near, approach (Jos.3:9, Jer.26:3 (Jer.46:3), al.): with dative, Acts.27:27 (WH, προσαχεῖν).†
 (AS)

G4318.d:
προσ-αγωγή, -ῆς, ἡ 
 (προσάγω), 
  1. a bringing to. 
  2. approach, access (see Lft., Notes, 284; MM, xxi): Rom.5:2, Eph.2:18 3:12 (but see Ellic., Eph., 59 f., where the transitive sense "introduction " is advocated).†
 (AS)

G4319.d:
προσ-αιτέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: Job.27:14 * ;] 
  1. to ask besides. 
  2. to continue asking; hence, to importune, beg, ask alms: John.9:8.†
 (AS)

G4320.d:
προσ-ανα-βαίνω 
 [in LXX: Exod.19:23, al. (עָלָה) ;] 
  1. to go up besides. 
  2. to go up higher: Luke.14:10.†
 (AS)

G4321.d:
προσ-αναλίσκω 
 to spend besides: Luke.8:43 (WH, R, mg., om.).†
 (AS)

G4322.d:
προσ-αναπληρόω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: Wis.19:4 * ;] 
to fill up by adding to, to supply fully: 2 Cor.9:12 11:9.†
 (AS)

G4323.d:
προσ-ανα-τίθημι 
 to lay on or offer besides; mid., 
  (a) to lay on oneself in addition, undertake besides; 
  (b) with genitive of person(s), of giving or obtaining information, to consult, communicate: Gal.1:16 2:6 (Lft., in l; cf. ἀνα-τίθημι) 
 (AS)

G4324.d:
προσ-απειλέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: Sir.13:3 א * ;] 
to threaten further: Acts.4:21.†
 (AS)

G4325.d:
προσδαπανάω, -ῶ 
 to spend besides: with accusative, Luke.10:35.†
 SYN.: προσαναλίσκω  (AS)

G4326.d:
προσ-δέομαι 
 [in LXX: Pro.12:9 חָסֵר חָסֵר Sir.6:1-37 * ;] 
to want further, need in addition: Acts.17:25.†
 (AS)

G4327.d:
προσ-δέχομαι 
 [in LXX chiefly for רָצָה ;] 
  1. to receive to oneself, receive favourably, admit, accept: with accusative of person(s), Luke.15:2, Rom.16:2, Phil.2:29; with accusative of thing(s), Acts.24:15 (R, mg.), Heb.10:34 11:35. 
  2. to expect, look for, wait for: with accusative of person(s), Luke.12:36; with accusative of thing(s), Mark.15:43, Luke.2:25, 38 23:51, Acts.23:21, Titus.2:13, Ju 21 (cf. δέχομαι).†
 (AS)

G4328.d:
προσ-δοκάω, -ῶ
 (the simple verb exists only in the forms δοκέω, -εύω) [in LXX: Ps.104:27 (שָׂבַר pi.), etc. ;] 
to await, expect: Matt.24:50, Luke.3:15 12:46, Acts.27:33 28:6; with accusative of person(s), Matt.11:3, Luke.1:21 7:19-20 8:40 Acts.10:24; with accusative of thing(s), 2 Pet.3:12-14; with accusative and inf., Acts.28:6; with inf., Acts.3:5.†
 (AS)

G4329.d:
προσδοκία, -ας, ἡ
 (ιροσδοκάω), [in LXX: Gen.49:10 (יִקָּהָה), Ps.119:116 (שֵׂבֶר) Wis.17:13, Sir.40:2, al. ;] 
expectation: with genitive obj., Luke.21:26; with genitive subjc., Acts.12:11.†
 (AS)

G4330.d: to suffer to go further , τινά (New Testament) (ML)

G4331.d:
προσ-εγγίζω 
 [in LXX chiefly for נָגַשׁ, קָרַב ;] 
  1. trans., to bring near (Luc.). 
  2. Intrans., to approach: with dative, Mark.2:4 (WH, προσενέγκαι).†
 (AS)

G4332.d:
προσεδρεύω
 (πρόσεδρος, sitting near), [in LXX: 1Ma.11:40 * ;] 
  1. to sit near. 
  2. to attend regularly: with dative, 1 Cor.9:13, Rec. (see: παρεδρεύω).†
 παρ-εδρεύω 
 [in LXX: Pro.1:21 8:3 * ;] 
to sit constantly beside, attend constantly (cf. MM, xix): τ. θυσιαστηρίω, 1 Cor.9:13.†
 (AS)

G4333.d:
προσ-εργάζομαι 
  1. to work or do service besides (Hdt., Plut.). 
  2. to gain besides, by working or trading: Luke.19:16 (Xen.).†
 (AS)

G4334.d:
προσ-έρχομαι 
 [in LXX for קָרַב, נָגַשׁ, etc. ;] 
to approach, draw near: absol., Matt.4:11, Luke.9:42, al.; with infin., Matt.24:1, al.; with dative loc., Heb.12:18, 22; dative of person(s), Matt.5:1, and freq., John.12:21, al.; ptcp., προσελθών, with indic., Matt.8:2, and freq., Mark.1:31, Luke.7:14, al.; π. αὐτῷ, with indic., Matt.4:3, Mark.6:35, 
 Metaphorical, 
  (a) of approaching God: absol. (Lev.21:17, Deu.21:5, al.), Heb.10:1, 22; τ. θεῷ, Heb.7:25 11:6; τ. θρόνῳ τ. χάριτος, Heb.4:16; πρὸς Χριστόν, 1 Pet.2:4; 
  (b) in sense not found elsewhere (Field, Notes, 211), to consent to: ὑγιαίνουσι λόγοις, 1 Tim.6:3 
 (AS)

G4335.d:
προσ-ευχή, -ῆς, ἡ
 (προσεύχομαι), [in LXX chiefly for תְּפִלָּה ;] 
  1. prayer to God: Matt.17:21 (WH, R, txt., om.) Matt.21:22, Mark.9:29, Luke.22:45, Acts.3:1 6:4 10:31, Rom.12:12, 1 Cor.7:5, Col.4:2; pl., Acts.2:42 10:4, Rom.1:10, Eph.1:16 Col.4:12, 1 Thess.1:2, Phm 4 22, 1 Pet.3:7 4:7, Rev.5:8 8:3-4; οἶκος προσευχῆς, Matt.21:13, Mark.11:17, Luke.19:46" (LXX) ; π. καὶ δέησις, Eph.6:18, Phil.4:6; pl., 1 Tim.2:1 5:5; ἡ π. τοῦ θεοῦ, prayer to God (ef. Wis.16:28), Luke.6:12; πρὸς τ. θεόν, before ὑπέρ, Acts.12:5; pl., Rom.15:30; Hebraistically (B1., § 38, 3), προσευχῇ προσεύχεσθαι, Jas.5:17 (EV, prayed fervently). 
  2. a place of prayer: of a synagogue (3Ma.7:20, seel.; see Charles, APOT, i, 173; for other exx., see Kennedy, Sources, 114); of a place in the open (FlJ, Ant., xiv, 10, 23), Acts.16:13, 16.†
 SYN.: see: δέησις  (AS)

G4336.d:
προσ-εύχομαι 
 [in LXX chiefly for פָּלַל hith. ;] 
to pray (always of prayer to God, or in cl., to gods): absol., Matt.6:5-7, 9 14:23 19:13 26:36, 39 26:41, 44, Mark.1:35 6:46 11:24-25 13:33 (WH, E, txt., om.) Mark.14:32, 38-39 Luke.1:10 3:21 5:16 6:12 9:18, 28-29 11:1-2 18:1, 10 22:44 (WH, E, mg., om.), Acts.1:24 6:6 9:11 10:9, 30 11:5 12:12 13:3 14:23 16:25 20:36 21:5 22:17 28:8, 1 Cor.11:4-5 14:14, 1 Thess.5:17, 1 Tim.2:8, Jas.5:13, 18; before λέγων, Matt.26:39, 42, Luke.22:41; with dative instr., 1 Cor.11:5 14:14-15; μακρά, Matt.23:14 (WH, R, txt., om.), Mark.12:40, Luke.20:47; ἐν πνεύματι (ἁγίῳ), Eph.6:18, Ju 20; προσευχῇ π. (a Hebraism, see: προσευχή), Jas.5:17; with accusative of thing(s), Luke.18:11, Rom.8:26; before ἐπί, with accusative of person(s), Jas.5:14; with dative of person(s), Matt.6:6, 1 Cor.11:13; before περί, with genitive, Acts.8:15, Col.1:3 4:3, 1 Thess.5:25, 2 Thess.1:11 3:1, Heb.13:18; ὑπέρ, Matt.5:44 Luke.6:28, Col.1:9, Jas.5:16; before ἵνα, Matt.24:20, Mark.13:18 14:35, Luke.22:46, 1 Cor.14:13; τοῦτο ἵνα, Phil.1:9; with inf., Luke.22:46; before τοῦ, with inf. (Bl., § 71, 3), Jas.5:17.†
 (AS)

G4337.d:
προσ-έχω 
 [in LXX for קָשַׁב hi., שָׁמַר ni., etc. ;] 
  1. to turn to, bring to (frequently ναῦν, expressed or understood, to bring to port, land; Hdt., al.). 
  2. τ. νοῦν, before dative, to turn one's mind to, attend to; in Xen. and later writers with νοῦν omitted (El., § 53, 1; 81, 1): Acts.8:6 16:14, Heb.2:1, 2 Pet.1:19; in sense of caring or providing for, Acts.20:28; π. ἑαυτῷ, to give heed to oneself (M, Pr., 157; cf. Gen.24:6, Exod.10:28, al.): Luke.17:3 21:34, Acts.5:35; id. before ἀπό (M, Pr., 102; B1., § 34, 11; 40, 3; see: βλέπω), Luke.12:1; (without dative) Matt.7:15 10:17 16:6, 11-12, Luke.20:46 (cf. Sir.6:13, al.); before μή, with inf. (M, Pr., 193; Bl., § 69, 4), Matt.6:1. 
  3. to attach or devote oneself to: with dative of person(s), Acts.8:10-11, 1 Tim.4:1; with dative of thing(s), 1 Tim.1:4 3:8 4:13 6:3 T (-ερχ-, WH, R), Titus.1:14, Heb.7:13.†
 (AS)

G4338.d:
προσ-ηλόω -ῶ 
 [in LXX: 3Ma.4:9 * ;] 
to nail to: with accusative and dative, figuratively, Col.2:14.†
 (AS)

G4339.d:
προσήλυτος, -ον
 (προοελαύνω), [in LXX for גֵּר ;] 
  1. one who has arrived, a stranger. 
  2. Of converts to Judaism, a proselyte (see DB, see word): Matt.23:15, Acts.2:10 6:5 13:43.†
 (AS)

G4340.d:
πρόσ-καιρος, -ον 
 [in LXX: 4Ma.15:2 4Mac 15:8 4Mac 15:23 * ;] 
  1. in season. 
  2. for a season, temporary, transient: 2 Cor.4:18, Heb.11:25; of plants, short-lived: Matt.13:21, Mark.4:17.†
 (AS)

G4341.d:
προσ-καλέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX chiefly for קָרָא ;] 
to call to. Mid., to call to oneself (see M, Pr., 157): with accusative of person(s), Matt.10:1, Mark.3:13 6:7, Luke.7:19, Acts.5:40, Jas.5:14, al. Metaphorical, of the Divine call: Acts.2:39; with inf., Acts.16:10 (see Bl., § 69, 4); before εἰς, Acts.13:2.†
 (AS)

G4342.d:
προσ-καρτερέω, -ῶ
 (καρτερός, strong, stedfast) [in LXX: Num.13:21 (חָזַק hith.), Tob.5:8 א, Da Th Su 1:6* ;] 
to attend constantly, continue stedfastly, adhere to, wait on: with dative of person(s), Mark.3:9, Acts.8:13 10:7; with dative of thing(s), Acts.1:14 2:42 6:4, Rom.12:12, Col.4:2; before ἐν, Acts.2:46; εἰς, Rom.13:6.†
 (AS)

G4344.d:
προσ-κεφάλαιον, -ου, τό 
 [in LXX: Eze.13:18, 20 (כֶּסֶת), I Est.3:8 * ;] 
a pillow, cushion: Mark.4:38.†
 (AS)

G4345.d:
προσ-κληρόω, -ῶ 
 to allot to, assign to by lot; pass. (but perh. as nid., EV, consorted with, so Syr.): Acts.17:4 (for exx., v, Cremer, 749).†
 (AS)

G4347.d:
προσ-κολλάω, -ῶ, 
 [in LXX chiefly for דָּבַק ;] 
to glue to; pass., reflexive, to stick to, cleave to (Plat.): metaphorically (with dative, Jos.23:8, Sir.6:34 al.), before πρός, Mark.10:7 (R, txt.), Eph.5:31 (LXX).†
 (AS)

G4348.d:
πρόσ-κομμα, -τος, τό
 (προσκόπτω), [in LXX: Exod.23:33 34:12 (מוֹקֵשׁ), Isa.8:14 (נֶגֶף), Jdth.8:22, Sir.17:25, al. ;] 
  (a) a stumble, stumbling: λίθος προσκόμματος (= נֶגֶף אֶבֶן, Isa, l.with), figuratively, Rom.9:32-33, 1 Pet.2:8" (LXX) ; 
  (b) = προσκοπή, an occasion of stumbling, a stumbling-block: metaphorically, Rom.14:13, 20, 1 Cor.8:9 (Plut.).†
 SYN.: σκάνδαλον (cf. Cremer, 752 f.)  (AS)

G4349.d:
προσκοπή, -ῆς, ή
 (προσκόπτω), [in Gr. Ven.: Pro.16:18 (כִּשָּׁלוֹן) * ;] 
an occasion of stumbling, offence: 2 Cor.6:3.†
 (AS)

G4350.d:
προσ-κόπτω 
 [in LXX for נָגַף, כָּשַׁל ni., etc. ;] 
  1. trans., to strike (e.g. hand or foot) against: with accusative before πρός, figuratively, Matt.4:6, Luke.4:11, (LXX) 
  2. Intrans., to stumble: absol. (Tob.11:9, Pro.3:23), John.11:9-10; of wind, to rush against, beat upon: with dative, Matt.7:27. Metaphorical, in late writers, 
  (a) to offend (Polyb.); 
  (b) to take offence at, stumble at: before ἐν, Rom.14:21; with dative, τ. λόγῳ, 1 Pet.2:8; τ. λίθῳ τ. προσκόμματος, Rom.9:32.†
 (AS)

G4351.d:
προσ-κυλίω 
 to roll up, roll to: with accusative and dative, Matt.27:60; accusative before ἐπί, Mark.15:46.†
 (AS)

G4354.d:
προσ-λαλέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: Exod.4:16 AB2 (דָבַר pi.), Wis.13:17 * ;] 
to speak to: Acts.28:20; with dative of person(s), Acts.13:43.†
 (AS)

G4355.d:
προσ-λαμβάνω 
 [in LXX: Ps.18:16 (מָשָׁה hi.), Ps.73:24 (לָקַח), etc. ;] 
  1. to take in addition. 
  2. to take to oneself, take, receive; in NT always mid., -ομαι; 
  (a) of things: of food, with accusative, Acts.27:33; with genitive part., Acts.27:36; 
  (b) of persons: with accusative, Matt.16:22, Mark.8:32 (see Swete, in l), Acts.17:5 18:26 28:2, Rom.14:1, 3 15:7, Phm 17.†
 (AS)

G4356.d:
πρόσ-λημψις (Rec. -ληψις, as in Att..), -εως, ἡ 
 (προσλαμβάνω), 
  1. an assumption (Plat.). 
  2. a receiving (cf. προσλαμβάνω): Rom.11:15,†
 (AS)

G4357.d:
προσ-μένω 
 [in LXX: Jdg.3:25 A (חוּל hi.), Tob.2:2 א, Wis.3:9, 3Ma.7:17 * ;] 
  1. to wait longer, continue, remain still: Acts.18:18; before ἐν, 1 Tim.1:3. 
  2. C. dative, to remain with: Matt.15:32, Mark.8:32. Metaphorical, to remain attached to, cleave unto, abide in: τ. κυρίῳ, Acts.11:23 (R, txt.; ἐν τ. κ., R, mg., see supr.); τ. χάριτι τ. θεοῦ, Acts.13:43; τ. δεήσεσιν, 1 Tim.5:5.†
 (AS)

G4358.d:
προσ-ορμίζω
 (ὅρμος, an anchorage), 
to bring a ship to anchor at; usually in mid., to come to anchor near, and so pass. in late writers (Ael., Dio Cass.): Mark.6:53.†
 (AS)
