G4360.d:
προσ-οχθίζω 
 [in LXX: Lev.26:15, al. (גָּעַל); Lev.18:25, al. (קוֹא), Ps.95:10, Eze.36:31 (קוּט), Sir.6:25, al. (other writers use ὀχθέω, rarely -ίζω) ;] 
to be angry with: with dative, Heb.3:10 (LXX), Heb.3:17.†
 (AS)

G4362.d:
προσ-πήγνυμι 
 to fasten to: absol., to crucify, Acts.2:23.†
 (AS)

G4363.d:
προσ-πίπτω
 [in LXX for נָפַל, נָגַע hi., כָּרַע ;] 
  1. to fall upon, strike against: with dative, of wind, Matt.7:25. 
  2. to fall down at one's feet, fall prostrate before: absol., before πρός, Mark.7:25; with dative of person(s), Mark.3:11 5:33, Luke.8:28, Acts.16:29; τ. γόνασιν, Luke.5:8.†
 (AS)

G4364.d:
προσ-ποιέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: 1Ki.21:13 (14) (הָלַל hithpo.), Job.19:14, (Sir 34:30 (Sir.31:30)), Dan LXX Su 1:11 * ;] 
to make over to, add or attach to. Mid., to take to oneself, claim; hence, to pretend; with inf. (cf. Xen., Anab., iv, 3, 20), to make as if: Luke.24:28.†
 (AS)

G4365.d:
προσ-πορεύομαι 
 [in LXX for קָרַב, נָגַשׁ, etc. ;] 
to come near, approach: with dative of person(s), Mark.10:35.†
 (AS)

G4367.d:
προσ-τάσσω 
 [in LXX chiefly for צָוָה pi. ;] 
  1. with accusative of person(s), to place at, to attach to. 
  2. to give a command, enjoin, appoint: Luke.5:14; with dative of person(s), Matt.1:24; with accusative of thing(s), Matt.8:4, Mark.1:44; with accusative and inf., Acts.10:48; pass., Acts.10:33 17:26.†
 (AS)

G4368.d:
προστάτις, -ιδος, ἡ
 (fem, of προοτάτης), 
a patroness, protectress: Rom.16:2.†
 (AS)

G4369.d:
προσ-τίθημι 
 [in LXX chiefly for יָסַף hi., also for אָסַף ni., etc. ;] 
  1. to put to. 
  2. to add, join to, give in addition: with accusative before ἐπί, Matt.6:27, Luke.3:20 12:25; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, Acts.2:47; with accusative and dative, Luke.17:5, Heb.12:19 (see MM, xxi); pass., absol., Acts.2:41, Gal.3:19; with dative, Matt.6:33, Mark.4:24, Luke.12:31, Acts.5:14 11:24; προσιτέθη πρὸς τ. πατέρας (cf. Gen.26:8, Jdg.2:10, al.), Acts.13:36; with inf., of repeating or continuing the action signified by the following verb, as in Heb. idiom (Gen.4:2 8:12, al.; cf. WM, § 54, 5; Lft. on Clem., 1Co., xii; but see also M, Pr., 67, 233; Deiss., BS, 67.1; MM, xxi), Luke.20:11, Acts.12:3; similarly ptcp., προσ-θείς, with indic. (Gen.38:5, al.), Luke.19:11.†
 (AS)

G4370.d:
προσ-τρέχω 
 [in LXX for רוּץ ;] 
to run to: Mark.9:15 10:17, Acts.8:30.†
 (AS)

G4371.d:
προσφάγιον, -ου, τό
 (φαγεῖν), 
Hellenistic for ὄψον ὀψάριον) 
 a relish or dainty (esp, cooked fish), to be eaten with bread: John.21:5  (have ye taken any fish, Field, Notes, 109; Abbott, Essays, 105; cf. M, Pr., 170n; MM, Exp., xxi).†
 (AS)

G4372.d:
πρόσφατος, -ον
 (on the derivation, see Boisacq, see word and cf. -ως), [in LXX: Num.6:3 (לַח), Deu.32:17, Ecc.1:9 (חָדָשׁ), Ps.81:9 (זוּר), Sir.9:10 * ;] 
  1. originally, freshly slain. 
  2. Generally (from Æsch. on), new, fresh, recent: ὁδός, Heb.10:20 (see MM, Exp., xxi; Rutherford, NPhr., 471 f.).†
 (AS)

G4373.d:
προσφάτως
  adv. (see: πρόσφατος), [in LXX: Deu.24:5 (חָדָשׁ), Jdth.4:3, 5, Eze.11:3, 2Ma.14:36 2Mac 14:16 ;] 
recently: Acts.18:2 (see MM, Exp., xxi).†
 (AS)

G4374.d:
προσ-φέρω 
 [in LXX chiefly for קָרַב hi. ;] 
  1. to bring to, lead to: with accusative and dative of person(s), Matt.4:24 8:16 9:2, 32 14:35 17:16, Mark.2:4 (WH, R, txt.; sc. αὐτόν) Mark.10:13, Luke.18:15 23:14; pass., Matt.12:22 (act., WH, txt.) Matt.18:24 (προσήχθη, WH) Matt.19:13; with accusative of thing(s), Matt.25:20; id. with dative of person(s), Matt.22:19, Luke.23:36; τ. στόματι, John.19:29; metaphorically, with dative of person(s), to deal with, Heb.12:7 (cl.). 
  2. to offer: Matt.2:11, Acts.8:18; esp. (as frequently in LXX; cf. FlJ, Ant., iii, 9, 3) sacrifices, gifts and prayers to God: absol., before περί (ὑπέρ), Mark.1:44, Luke.5:14, Heb.5:1, 3 9:7 10:12; pass., Acts.21:26; with accusative of thing(s) (δῶρον, θυσίαν, λυτρείαν, προσφοράν), Matt.5:23-24 (aoristic pres.; M, Pr., 247) Matt.8:4, John.16:2, Acts.7:42 21:26, Heb.5:1 8:3-4 9:7, 9 10:1-2, 8 10:11-12; δεήσεις τε κ. ἱκετηρίας, Heb.5:7; with accusative of person(s), Heb.11:17 (conative impf.; M, Pr., 129); of Christ, Heb.7:27 (ἀνενέγκας, WH, txt.) Heb.9:14, 25 9:28.†
 (AS)

G4375.d:
προσφιλής, -ές
 (φιλέω), [in LXX: Est.5:1, Sir.4:7 20:13 * ;] 
  (a) of persons, in both act, and pass. sense (LXX, ll. with); 
  (b) of things, pleas­ing, agreeable (EV, lovely): Phil.4:8.†
 (AS)

G4376.d:
προσ-φορά, -ᾶς, ἡ
 (προσφέρω), [in LXX: 3Ki.7:48 (פָּנִים) Ps.40:6 (מִנְחָה), I Est.5:52, Sir.14:11, al. ;] 
  1. a bringing to, offering (Plat., al.). 
  2. (Less frequently in cl.), a present, an offering; in NT, of sacrificial offerings: Acts.21:26 24:17, Eph.5:2, Heb.10:5, 8 10:14; περί ἀμαρτίας, Heb.10:18; with genitive obj., Rom.15:16, Heb.10:10.†
 (AS)

G4377.d:
προσ-φωνέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX: 1Es.2:21 Est.6:6 Est.6:22, 2Ma.15:15 * ;] 
  1. to address, call to; in cl., with accusative of person(s), with dupl. accusative (cf. 2Mac, l.with); absol. (Hom., Od., v, 159, al.): Acts.21:40 In late writers, with dative of person(s): Matt.11:16, Luke.7:32 13:12 23:20, Acts.22:2. 
  2. to call by name, summon: with accusative (as in cl.), Luke.6:13.†
 (AS)

G4378.d:
πρόσ-χυσις, -εως, ἡ 
 a pouring or sprinkling upon: Heb.11:28.†
 (AS)

G4379.d:
προσ-ψαύω 
 in poët. and late writers, 
 to touch: with dative, Luke.11:46.†
 (AS)

G4380.d:
προσωπολημπτέω (Rec. -ληπτ-), -ῶ 
 (-λήμπτης, which see), 
to have respect of persons: Jas.2:9.†
 (AS)

G4381.d:
προσωπο-λήμπτης (Rec. -λήπτης, see Bl., § 6, 8), -ου, ὁ 
 (πρόσωπον λαμβάνειν, see: πρόσωπον), 
a respecter of persons: Acts.10:34 (on this group of cognate forms, see Mayor, da., 78 f.; and cf. Thackeray, Gr., 44).†
 (AS)

G4382.d:
προσωπολημψία (Rec. -ληψία), -ας, ἡ 
 (προσωπολήμπτης) 
respect of persons: Rom.2:11, Eph.6:9, Col.3:25, Jas.2:1 (see Mayor, in l).†
 (AS)

G4383.d:
πρόσωπον, -ου, τό
 (πρός, ὤψ), [in LXX chiefly and very frequently for פָּנִים ;] 
  1. prop., of persons (so always in cl.); 
  (a) the face, countenance:  Matt.6:16-17, Mark.14:65, Luke.9:29, 2 Cor.3:7, Rev.4:7, al.; τὸ π. τῆς γενέτεως (EV, natural face), Jas.1:23; πίπτειν ἐπὶ (τὰ) π., Matt.17:6, Luke.5:12, Rev.7:11, al.; ἀγνοούμενος τῷ π., Gal.1:22; π., οὐ καρδίᾳ, 1 Thess.2:17; κατὰ πρόσωπον (in front, facing: Thuc., Xen., al.), when present, face to face, Acts.25:16, 2 Cor.10:1 10:7, Gal.2:11; id. with genitive, as compound prep., in the presence of (not cl.; see Bl., § 40, 9; M, Pr., 99 f.; Thackeray, Gr., 43 f.), Luke.2:31, Acts.3:13; similarly ἀπὸ π. (Heb. (פָּנִים מִלִּפְּנֵי); see Dalman, Words, 29), from the presence of, Acts.3:19 5:41 7:45, 2 Thess.1:9, Rev.12:14 20:11; πρὸ π. (Heb. (פָּנִים לִפְנֵי), before, Matt.11:10, Mark.1:2, Luke.7:27" (LXX), al.; in other phrases resembling Heb. idiom (Thackeray, Gr., 42), βλέπειν (ὁρᾶν, θεωρεῖν, ἰδεῖν) τὸ π., to see one's face, i.e. see him in person, Matt.18:10, Acts.20:25, 38, 1 Thess.3:10, Rev.22:4; ἐμφανισθῆναι τῷ π. τοῦ θεοῦ, Heb.9:24; ἐν π. Χριστοῦ, 2 Cor.2:10 4:6; μετὰ τοῦ π. σου with thy presence, Acts.2:28 (LXX); εἰς π. τῶν ἐκκλησιῶν, 2 Cor.8:24; στηρίζειν τὸ π. (Heb. פָּנִים שׂוּם: Jer.21:10, al.; see Dalman, Words, 30), with inf., to set one's face towards, Luke.9:51; similarly, τὸ π. αὐτοῦ ἦν πορευόμενον (op. cit., 31), Luke.9:53; τὸ π. τοῦ κυρίου ἐπί, 1 Pet.3:12 (LXX) 
  (b) form, person: καυχᾶσθαι. ἐν π. καὶ μὴ ἐν καρδίᾳ, 2 Cor.5:12 (cf. 1Ki.16:7); metaphorically, as in Heb. idiom, of judgment according to appearance, external condition or circumstances (פָּנִים H5387; see Dalman, Words, 30; Thackeray, Gr., 43 f.): λαμβάνειν π., Luke.20:21, Gal.2:6; βλέπειν εἰς π., Matt.22:16, Mark.12:14; θαυμάζειν πρόσωπα, Ju 16. 
  2. Of things (cf. Dalman, l.with) 
  (a) face, appearance (Ps.104:30): Matt.16:3 (WH, R, mg., om.), Luke.12:56, Jas.1:11 
  (b) surface (Gen.2:6): Luke.21:35, Acts.17:26 
 (AS)

G4384.d:
προ-τάσσω 
 [in LXX: 2Ma.8:36 R (Α, προστ-) * ;] 
  1. to place in front. 
  2. to arrange beforehand: Acts.17:26, Rec. (for προστ., Edd.).†
 (AS)

G4385.d:
προ-τείνω, [in LXX: 2Ma_7:1-42, 3Ma_2:1 * ;]
 to stretch out, stretch forth: of preparations for scourging (see Field, Notes, 136 f.), Acts.22:25.†
 (AS)

G4386.d:
before; (adv.) before, formerly, an earlier time 
former, prior, Eph. 4:22; before, former, prior, Eph. 4:22; before, formerly, Jn. 6:62

G4387.d:
A. Compar., πρότερος, -α, -ον, 
 [in LXX for רִאשׁוֹן ,לִפָנִים, etc. ;] 
before, of time, place, rank, etc.; in NT always of Time, before, former: Eph.4:22. Adverbially, πρότερον, before, aforetime, formerly: John.7:50, 2 Cor.1:15, Heb.4:6; opposite to ἔπειτα, Heb.7:27; τὸ π., John.6:62 9:8, Gal.4:13, 1 Tim.1:13; αἱ π. ἡμέραι, Heb.10:32; αἱ π. ἐπιθυμίαι, 1 Pet.1:14.† 
 (AS)

G4388.d:
προ-τίθημι 
 [in LXX: Exod.40:4, 23, Lev.24:8 (עָרַךְ) Ps.54:3 (שׂוּם), etc. ;] 
  1. to set before, set forth publicly; so also in mid.: with accusative of person(s), Rom.3:25 (for a suggested alt, rend., see MM, xxii). 
  2. Mid., to set before oneself, propose, purpose: with inf., Rom.1:13; with accusative of thing(s), Eph.1:9.†
 (AS)

G4389.d:
προ-τρέπω 
 [in LXX: Wis.14:18, 2Ma.11:7, 4Ma.12:7 4Mac 15:12 4Mac 16:13 * ;] 
to urge forwards, exhort, persuade. Mid., in same sense (as also in cl.): Acts.18:27.†
 (AS)

G4390.d:
προ-τρέχω 
 [in LXX: 1Ki.8:11 (פָּנִים רוּץ), Job.41:13 (14) A (דּוּץ), Tob.11:3 (before ἔμπροσθεν), 1Ma.16:21 * ;] 
  1. to run forward. 
  2. to run on, run in advance: John.20:4; before εἰς τὸ ἔμπροσθεν, Luke.19:4.†
 (AS)

G4391.d:
προ-ϋπ-άρχω 
 [in LXX: Job 42:18* ;] 
  1. to be beforehand in. 
  2. to be before or previously: with ptcp., Luke.23:12, Acts.8:9.†
 (AS)

G4392.d:
πρό-φασις, -εως, ἡ
 (φήμι), [in LXX: Ps.141:4 (עֲלִילָה), ??עֲלִילָה), ??Dan.6:4-5(5-6) (עִלָּה) Pro.18:1, Hos.10:4 * ;] 
a pretence, pretext: Matt.23:1 (WM, R, txt., om.), Mark.12:40, Luke.20:47 John.15:22, Acts.27:30, Phil.1:18, 1 Thess.2:5.†
 (AS)

G4393.d:
προφέρω 
 [in LXX: Pro.10:13 (מָצָא ni.), Tob.9:5, al. ;] 
to bring forth: with accusative of thing(s), before ἐκ, Luke.6:45.†
 (AS)

G4394.d:
προφητεία, -ας, ἡ
 (προψητεύω) [in LXX for נְבוּאָה, חָזוֹן ;] 
the gift (and its exercise) of interpreting the Divine will and purpose, prophecy, prophesying: of OT prophecy, Matt.13:14, 2 Pet.1:20-21; of NT prophecy, Rom.12:6, 1 Cor.12:10 13:2 14:6 14:22, 1 Tim.4:14, Rev.11:6 22:19; pl., 1 Cor.13:8, 1 Thess.5:20, 1 Tim.1:18; οἱ λόγοι τῆς π., Rev.1:3 22:7, 10 22:18; τ. πνεῦμα τῆς π., Rev.19:10 (Luc., FlJ, LXX, π.; see Deiss., BS, 235 f.; MM, xxii).†
 (AS)

G4395.d:
προφητεύω
 (προφήτης), [in LXX chiefly for נָבָא ni., hith. ;] 
to be a προφήτης (which see), to prophesy: in the primary sense of telling forth the Divine counsels, Matt.7:22 26:68, Mark.14:65, Luke.1:67 22:64, Acts.19:6, 1 Cor.11:4-5 13:9 14:1 14:3-5 14:24 14:31 14:39, Heb.11:3; with the idea of foretelling future events (an idea merely incidental, not essential; see Lft., Notes, 83 f.), Matt.11:13, Acts.2:17-18" (LXX) Acts.21:9; before περί, Matt.15:7, Mark.7:6, 1 Pet.1:10; ἐπί, with dative, Rev.10:11; λέγων, Ju 14; ὅτι, John.11:51.†
 SYN.: μαντεύομαι, q.v  (AS)

G4397.d:
προφητικός, -ά, -όν
 (προφήτης), 
of prophecy, prophetic: Rom.16:26, 2 Pet.1:19.†
 (AS)

G4398.d:
προφῆτις, -ιδος, ἡ fem, of προφήτης, 
 [in LXX: Exod.15:20, Jdg.4:4, 4Ki.22:14, 2Ch.34:22, Isa.8:3 (נְבִיאָה) * ;] 
a prophetess: Luke.2:36, Rev.2:20.†
 (AS)

G4399.d:
προ-φθάνω 
 [in LXX chiefly for קָדַם pi. ;] 
with ptcp. (as in cl., but more frequently the simple φθάνω, which see), 
 to anticipate: Matt.17:25.†
 (AS)

G4400.d:
προ-χειρίζω
 (πρόχειρος, at hand) [in LXX: Exod.4:13 (שָׁלַח), Jos.3:12 (לָקַח), Dan LXX 3:22, 2Ma.3:7 2Mac 8:9 2Mac 14:12 A * ;] 
  1. to put into the hand, deliver up: pass., Acts.3:20. 
  2. More frequently as depon., -ομαι, to take into one's hand; hence, metaphorically, to propose, determine, choose: with inf., Acts.22:14; with accusative of person(s), Acts.26:16.†
 (AS)

G4401.d:
προ-χειρο-τονέω, -ῶ
 (see χειροτονέω) 
to choose or appoint beforehand: Acts.10:41 (Plat., al.).†
 (AS)

G4403.d:
πρύμνα, -ης, ἡ 
 prop. fem. of adj. πρύμνο, -η, -ον, (sc. ναῦς), the hindmost part of a ship, the stern: Mark.4:38, Acts.27:29; opposite to πρῷρα, Acts.27:41.†
 (AS)

G4404.d:
πρωί (Rec. πρωΐ), 
 adv.  (πρό), [in LXX chiefly for בֹּקֶר ;] 
in the morning, early: Matt.16:3 (R, txt.) Matt.21:18, Mark.1:35 11:20 13:35 15:1, John.18:28 20:1; λίαν π., Mark.16:2; ἅμα π., Matt.20:1; ἀπὸ π. (cf. ἀπὸ πρωΐθεν, Exod.18:13), Acts.28:23.† 
 (AS)

G4405.d:
πρώιος (Rec. -ϊος), -α, -ον 
 (πρωί), [in LXX for בֹּקֶר בַּ לַּ ;] 
at early morn, early; as subst., ἡ π. (sc. ὥρα, cf. ἡ ὥ. ἡ π., 3Ma.5:24), early morning: Matt.27:1, John.21:4.†
 (AS)

G4406.d:
πρώϊμος, see: πρόϊμος .
  πρόϊμος (Rec. πρώ-, of which προ- is a late form; see Bl., § 6, 4; WH, App., 152), -ον, 
 [in LXX: Deu.11:14 (יוֹרֶה), etc. ;] 
= the more common πρώιος (which see), 
 early: of rain (as most frequently in LXX), Jas.5:7.†
 (AS)

G4407.d:
πρωινός
 (Rec. -ϊνος, see WH, App., ή, -όν (πρωί), [in LXX chiefly for בֹּקֶר ;] 
= cl. πρώιος, 
 at early morn, early: ἀστήρ, Rev.2:28 22:16.†
 (AS)

G4408.d:
πρῷρα (Rec. incorrectly πρώρα, see Bl., § 3, 3; LS, see word), -ης (for Att.. -ας, see Bl., § 7, 1; Mayser, l 2), ἡ, 
 the forward part of a ship, the prow: Acts.27:30; opposite to πρύμνα, ib. Acts.27:41.†
 (AS)

G4409.d:
πρωτεύω
 (πρῶτος) [in LXX: Est.5:11, 2Ma.6:18 2Mac 13:15 * ;] 
to be first, pre-eminent, have the first place: Col.1:18.†
 (AS)

G4410.d:
πρωτοκαθεδρία, -ας, ἡ
 (πρῶιος, καθέδρα), 
the chief seat: Matt.23:6, Mark.12:39 (see Swete, in l), Luke.11:43 20:46.†
 (AS)

G4411.d:
πρωτο-κλυτία, -ας, ἡ 
 the chief place at table (see Swete, Mk., l.with): Matt.23:6, Mark.12:39, Luke.14:7-8 20:46.†
 (AS)

G4412.d:
πρῶτον, πρῶτος, see: πρότερος 
  A. Compar., πρότερος, -α, -ον, 
 [in LXX for רִאשׁוֹן ,לִפָנִים, etc. ;] 
before, of time, place, rank, etc.; in NT always of Time, before, former: Eph.4:22. Adverbially, πρότερον, before, aforetime, formerly: John.7:50, 2 Cor.1:15, Heb.4:6; opposite to ἔπειτα, Heb.7:27; τὸ π., John.6:62 9:8, Gal.4:13, 1 Tim.1:13; αἱ π. ἡμέραι, Heb.10:32; αἱ π. ἐπιθυμίαι, 1 Pet.1:14.† 
 (AS)

G4414.d:
πρωτοστάτης, -ου, ὁ
 (πρῶτος, ἵστημι) [in LXX: Job.15:24 AB * ;] 
prop., of soldiers, one who stands first, one in the front rank (Thuc., Xen.); hence, metaphorically, a leader: Acts.24:5.†
 (AS)

G4415.d:
πρωτοτόκια, -ων, τά
 (πρωτότοκος) [in LXX (with seel. -εῖα, -εία): Gen.25:31 ff. Gen.27:36, Deu.21:17, 1Ch.5:1 (בְּכוֹרָה) * ;] 
the rights of the first-born, birthright (= cl. ἡ πρεσβεία): Heb.12:16.†
 (AS)

G4416.d:
πρωτότοκος, -ον
 (πρῶτος, τίκτω) [in LXX chiefly for בְּכוֹר ;] 
first-born: Luke.2:7; pl., Heb.11:28. Metaphorical, of the priority of Christ (originally perh. a Messianic title, cf. Ps.89:28, Heb.1:6; see ICC on Col.1:15): Heb.1:6; π. πάσης κτίσεως, Col.1:15; ἐν πολλοῖς ἀδελφοῖς, Rom.8:29; π. (ἐκ) τ. νεκρῶν, Col.1:18, Rev.1:5; pl., of the elect, ἐκκλησία πρωτοτόκων, Heb.12:23.†
 (AS)

G4417.d:
πταίω 
 [in LXX chiefly for נָגַף ni. ;] 
  1. trans., to cause to stumble (1Ki.4:3, cf. Deiss., BS, 681). 
  2. Intrans., to stumble. Metaphorical, in moral sense, Rom.11:11, Jas.2:10 3:2, 2 Pet.1:10.†
 (AS)

G4418.d:
πτέρνα, -ης, ἡ 
 [in LXX for עָקֵב ;] 
the heel: figuratively, ἐπαίρειν τὴν π. ἐπί, John.13:18 (LXX).†
 (AS)

G4419.d:
πτερύγιον, -ου, -τό
 (dimin. of πτέρυξ), [in LXX chiefly for כָּנָף ;] 
  1. a little wing. 
  2. Anything like a wing, as a turret, battlement: τ. ἱεροῦ, Matt.4:5, Luke.4:9.†
 (AS)

G4420.d:
πτέρυξ, -υγος, ἡ
 (πέτομαι), [in LXX chiefly for כָּנָף ;] 
a wing: of birds, Matt.23:37, Luke.13:34, Rev.12:14; of creatures seen in a vision, Rev.4:8 9:9.†
 (AS)

G4421.d:
πτηνός, -ή, -όν
 (πέτομαι), [in Aq.: Job.5:7 * ;] 
winged; as subst., π., birds: 1 Cor.15:39.†
 (AS)

G4422.d:
πτοέω, -ῶ 
 [in LXX chiefly for חָתַת ni. ;] 
to terrify. Pass., to be terrified: Luke.21:9 24:37 (WH, mg., θροηθέντες).†
 (AS)

G4423.d:
πτόησις, -εως, ἡ
 (πτοέω) [in LXX: Pro.3:25 (פַּחַד), Sir 50:4 א1, 1Ma.3:25 R * ;] 
a fluttering, excitement, caused by any emotion, but esp. by fear, hence, terror: φοβεῖσθαι πτόησιν, to be afraid with (cogn. accusative) or of any terror (see ICC, in l): 1 Pet.3:6.†
 (AS)

G4424.d:
Πτολεμαΐς, -ΐδος, ἡ 
 Ptolemais, a maritime city of Phœnicea: Acts.21:7.†
 (AS)

G4425.d:
πτύον, -ου, τό 
 [in Sm.: Isa.30:24 * ;] 
a winnowing shovel or fan: Matt.3:12, Luke.3:17.†
 (AS)

G4426.d:
πτύρομαι  depon., 
 to be startled, frightened: Phil.1:28. (The active πτύρω is also found in some late writers.) †
 (AS)

G4427.d:
πτύσμα, -τος, τό,
 (πτύω) 
spittle: John.9:6 (Hipp., Polyb., al.).†
 (AS)

G4428.d:
πτύσσω 
 to fold; of a scroll, to roll up: βιβλίον, Luke.4:20 (cf. ἀνα-πτύσσω).†
 (AS)

G4429.d:
πτύω 
 [in LXX: Num.12:14 (יָרָק), Sir.28:12 * ;] 
to spit: Mark.7:33 8:23, John.9:6 (cf. ἐκ-, ἐμ-πτύω).†
 (AS)

G4430.d:
πτῶμα -τος, τό
 (πίπτω), [in LXX: Jdg.14:8 (מַפֶּלֶת), Job.16:15 (14) (פֶּרֶץ), Isa.51:19 (שֹׁד), Jdth.8:19, Wis.4:18, al. ;] 
  1. a fall, metaphorically, a misfortune, calamity (Trag., Plat., Polyb., al.; LXX). 
  2. That which has fallen; 
  (a) of buildings, a ruin (Polyb.); 
  (b) of living creatures, in cl. (poët. only) usually with genitive, νεκρῶν, etc., but also absol., as in late writers and NT, a fallen body, a carcase, corpse: Matt.14:12 24:28, Mark.15:45; π. αὐτοῦ, Mark.6:29; αὐτῶν, Rev.11:8-9 (cf. Rutherford, NPhr., 472 f.).†
 (AS)

G4431.d:
πτῶσις, -εως, ἡ
 (πίπτω), [in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶף, מַפֶּלֶת, and cogn. forms ;] 
a falling, fall (Plat., Plut., al.): Matt.7:27; metaphorically, Luke.2:34.†
 (AS)

G4432.d:
πτωχεία, -ας, ἡ
 (πτωχεύω), [in LXX chiefly for עֳנִי ;] 
beggary, destitution: 2 Cor.8:2 8:9, Rev.2:9.†
 (AS)

G4433.d:
πτωχεύω
 (πτωχός), [in LXX: Jdg.6:6, Ps.79:8 (דָּלַל); Jdg.14:15 A, Pro.23:21 (יָרַשׁ); Ps.34:10 (רוּשׁ), Tob.4:21 * ;] 
  1. to be a beggar, to beg (so chiefly in cl.). 
  2. to be poor as a beggar, to be destitute, poor: opposite to πλούσιος ὤν, 2 Cor.8:9.†
 (AS)

G4434.d:
πτωχός, -ή, -όν
 (πτώσσω, to crouch, cower), [in LXX for עָנִי, דַּל, רָשׁ, etc. ;] 
of one who crouches and cowers, hence, 
  1. as subst., a beggar: Luke.14:13, 21 16:20, 22. 
  2. As adj., 
  (a) prop., beggarly: metaphorically, στοιχεῖα, Gal.4:9 (see Lft., in l); 
  (b) in broader sense (opposite to πλούσιος), poor: Matt.11:5 19:21 26:9, 11, Mark.10:21 12:42-43 14:5, 7, Luke.4:18 7:22 18:22 19:8 21:3, John.12:5-6, 8 13:29, Rom.15:26, 2 Cor.6:10, Gal.2:10, Jas.2:2-3, 6, Rev.13:16; π. τ. κόσμῳ, Jas.2:5; metaphorically, Luke.6:20, Rev.3:17; π. τ. πνεύματι, Matt.5:3.†
 SYN.: πένης, q.v  (AS)

G4435.d:
πυγμή, -ῆς, ἡ 
 [in LXX: Exod.21:18, Isa.58:4 (אֶגְרֹף) * ;] 
the fist: πυγμῇ νίψασθαι τ. χῖρας (Τ, πυκνά; Vg., Goth., Copt., crebro), to wash the hands with the fist (diligently, R, txt.; up to the elbow, R, mg.; the exact meaning is doubtful; see Swete, in l): Mark.7:3.†
 (AS)

G4436.d:
πύθων, -ωνος, ὁ 
  1. in cl., Python, a serpent slain by Apollo, who is hence surnamed the Pythian. 
  2. In Plut. (ii, 414 E), a name given to ventriloquist soothsayers (ἐγγαστρίμυθοι; cf. Lev.19:31 20:6, 27, 1Ki.28:7), and perhaps in this sense πνεῦμα πύθωνα, a python-spirit: Acts.16:16.†
 (AS)

G4437.d:
πυκιός, -ή, -όν 
 [in LXX: Eze.31:3 A (חֹרֶשׁ), 3Ma.1:28 3Mac 4:10, 4Ma.12:12 * ;] 
  1. close, compact, solid. 
  2. frequent: 1 Tim.5:23. Neut. pl., πυκνά, as adv., much, often: Mark.7:3 Τ (see: πυγμή), Luke.5:33. Comparat., πυκνότερον, very often or so much the oftener (seeBl., § 44, 3,): Acts.24:26.†
 (AS)

G4438.d:
πυκτεύω
 (πύκτης, a pugilist), 
to box: 1 Cor.9:26.†
 (AS)

G4439.d:
